records.claim_title: Untrusted SVG can force Batik's default transcoder to load arbitrary external resources (SSRF / local file access) because the default UserAgent returns RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: UserAgentAdapter.getExternalResourceSecurity() returns a RelaxedExternalResourceSecurity instance whose checkLoadExternalResource() body is empty, i.e. every URI scheme and host is allowed. SVGAbstractTranscoder's user agent (SVGAbstractTranscoderUserAgent extends UserAgentAdapter) does not override this method, so the default used by ImageTranscoder/rasterizer accepts all external resources. Every bridge that resolves URI-valued SVG attributes then calls this no-op check before opening the stream (SVGImageElementBridge.createImageGraphicsNode -> openStream; URIResolver.getNode for use/tref/mpath/patterns/filters; SVGColorProfileElementBridge; FontFace; CSSEngine.parseStyleSheet), so an xlink:href/href value supplied by the SVG author is dereferenced without any effective origin/protocol restriction. The stricter DefaultExternalResourceSecurity that exists alongside it is not the library default and compares only host names (not scheme/port) anyway.

records.ground_truth_vulnerability: XmlConverter.toSAXSourceFromStream does not disable external-general-entities.
records.ground_truth: XmlConverter.toSAXSourceFromStream does not disable external-general-entities.
records.claim_title: XXE via camel-core XML converters/validators: external entity and DTD resolution not fully disabled for untrusted XML bodies
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Camel-core's shared XML parsing helpers create JAXP factories/validators with only partial XXE hardening. (1) XmlConverter.createDocumentBuilderFactory() disables only http://xml.org/sax/features/external-general-entities; external-parameter-entities and external DTD loading stay enabled and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is not set, so a crafted DOCTYPE with parameter entities/external DTD can still make the parser fetch attacker- or file-specified resources (blind file exfiltration/SSRF). (2) XmlConverter.toSAXSourceFromStream(), which builds the XMLReader used by every StreamSource/InputStream/String -> SAXSource conversion, sets only FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and no external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities/DTD restriction; on JAXP implementations/JDKs where secure processing does not restrict external access this resolves external general entities (classic file-read XXE). (3) ValidatingProcessor.createSchemaFactory() creates a SchemaFactory without FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING/access restrictions and getSource() hands the raw message body to Validator.validate() as a StreamSource, so the JAXP validator parses attacker XML with default external access.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Java deserialization of HTTP payloads in Camel HTTP components (request body and response body)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Camel's HTTP bindings treat the HTTP Content-Type header as the only gate for Java deserialization. Whenever Content-Type equals "application/x-java-serialized-object", the payload is passed to HttpHelper.deserializeJavaObjectFromStream(), which unconditionally calls new ObjectInputStream(is).readObject(). There is no allowJavaSerializedObject opt-in, no class allow-list/ObjectInputFilter, and no trust check anywhere in the snapshot; the camel-http/camel-http4 request binding is used by Jetty/Servlet/CamelServlet consumers, so the deserialization happens while the inbound message is populated, before any route-level authentication, validation, or choice logic runs. The producer path has the same problem for responses (it deserializes even when the endpoint's transferException option is disabled).

records.claim_title: Expander containment check bypassable via sibling directory sharing the target path prefix (path traversal / arbitrary file write outside target directory)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Expander.expand() resolves the entry target with new File(targetDirectory, entry.getName()) and validates containment with f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(targetDirectory.getCanonicalPath()). The canonical path of an entry whose name contains '../' is normalized (e.g. /srv/data/../data-backup/x -> /srv/data-backup/x), and a plain string prefix test accepts any path whose first characters match the target directory name, not just paths actually inside it. There is no File.separator/Path-component boundary in the comparison and no normalized Path.startsWith() check, so a sibling directory whose name begins with the target directory's name (target '/srv/data' vs sibling '/srv/data-backup') is treated as inside the target.

records.claim_title: Unbounded heap allocation driven by attacker-declared PAX header record length in TarArchiveInputStream
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: TarArchiveInputStream.parsePaxHeaders() parses the numeric 'length' field of a PAX extended header record from the archive data and then computes restLen = len - read, allocating new byte[restLen] without validating len against the PAX entry size, remaining record data, or any maximum. len is accumulated as an int with unchecked decimal multiplication/addition (len *= 10; len += ch - '0'), so a short PAX header can request a heap allocation of up to ~Integer.MAX_VALUE bytes (and int overflow can make restLen negative, producing a NegativeArraySizeException). The allocation occurs before IOUtils.readFully() can discover that the declared bytes are absent.

records.claim_title: Crafted 7z bind-pair chain causes infinite loop / unbounded memory growth in SevenZFile folder decoding
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Folder.getOrderedCoders() follows the bind-pair chain starting from packedStreams[0] with `while (current != -1) { l.addLast(coders[current]); current = pair != -1 ? (int) bindPairs[pair].inIndex : -1; }` and never checks that the chain terminates or that a coder/input index has already been visited. SevenZFile.readFolder() reads the bind pairs (inIndex/outIndex) straight from the archive header and only validates `totalOutStreams != 0` and `totalInStreams >= numBindPairs`; it does not require bind-pair indices to be unique, in range, or to form an acyclic chain. An archive whose bind pairs form a cycle (e.g. four simple coders with pairs out(0)->in(1), out(1)->in(2), out(2)->in(1) and packed stream 0) makes findBindPairForOutStream() return to the same input index forever, so the loop adds coders without bound.

records.claim_title: Default variable-interpolation lookups (script/url/dns/file) are enabled for every configuration and allow code execution, SSRF and local file disclosure from attacker-influenced configuration values
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: ConfigurationInterpolator builds its immutable default prefix-lookup map from DefaultLookups values (SCRIPT, URL, DNS, FILE, CONST, PROPERTIES, RESOURCE_BUNDLE, XML, ...) plus Commons Text DefaultStringLookup values, and AbstractConfiguration.installDefaultInterpolator() registers that whole set on every configuration instance unconditionally. ConfigurationInterpolator.resolve() dispatches ${prefix:name} straight to the registered lookup, and DefaultConversionHandler.to() interpolates string values during typed conversion. The library therefore treats configuration values as trusted interpolation expressions and exposes script execution, arbitrary URL fetching and file reading by default, with no opt-in or filtering.

records.claim_title: Unbounded multipart boundary length causes non-terminating zero-length-read loop in MultipartStream (CPU-exhaustion DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MultipartStream derives keepRegion and pad from the untrusted boundary length (boundaryLength = boundary.length + 4) without validating it against the fixed buffer size (DEFAULT_BUFSIZE = 4096). When boundaryLength > bufSize, ItemInputStream.makeAvailable() sets pad = tail - head = bufSize, so available() returns tail - head - pad = 0 while pos remains -1; the refill loop then repeatedly calls input.read(buffer, bufSize, 0), which returns 0 rather than -1, and tail/head/pad never change. The only exits are finding a separator (impossible, since maxpos = tail - boundaryLength is negative in findSeparator(), MultipartStream.java:697-718) or reading -1 (never returned for a zero-length read).

records.claim_title: Unbounded attacker-controlled multipart boundary can make MultipartStream loop forever (request-thread CPU exhaustion)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MultipartStream's public constructor (lines 323-344) stores the caller-supplied boundary and buffer size without enforcing that the buffer is larger than boundary.length + BOUNDARY_PREFIX.length + 1. It allocates buffer = new byte[bufSize] (line 329) and sets boundaryLength = keepRegion = boundary.length + 4 (lines 335-336), so an attacker who supplies a boundary of >= 4092 bytes makes keepRegion >= the default 4096-byte buffer. ItemInputStream.findSeparator() (lines 817-826) then sets pad = keepRegion / tail-head, which can equal bufSize; makeAvailable() (lines 983-1017) copies the keep region to the front, sets tail = pad = bufSize, and repeatedly executes input.read(buffer, tail, bufSize - tail) at line 997 with a zero-length read. Zero-length reads return 0 (never -1), findSeparator() returns -1, available() stays 0, and the `if (av > 0 || pos != -1)` exit at line 1013 is never satisfied, so the for(;;) loop spins at 100% CPU and never returns or throws.

records.claim_title: PNG IHDR 'InterlaceMethod' byte used as enum-array index; bounds check is dead because it uses && instead of ||
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In PngChunkIhdr the 13th byte of the attacker-supplied IHDR chunk is read as the interlace method and then used directly as an index into InterlaceMethod.values(). The intended guard is written as `if (method < 0 && method >= InterlaceMethod.values().length)`. No int can satisfy both comparands, so the guard is dead code and the array access at line 56 is completely unvalidated. Note the value is also sign-extended: BinaryFunctions.readByte returns `(byte)(0xff & result)`, so IHDR method bytes 0x80-0xFF become negative ints (e.g. 0xFF -> -1) and byte 0x02 stays 2; `InterlaceMethod` has only NONE(0) and ADAM7(1), so any value other than 0/1 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

records.claim_title: Character filter readers bypass character filtering on the bulk read(char[], int, int) path
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In AbstractCharacterFilterReader.read(char[] cbuf, int off, int len) the compaction loop tests `filter(read)`, i.e. it passes the number of characters returned by the delegate read instead of the character at the current position (`filter(cbuf[readPos])`). Because `read` is constant for the whole call, the outcome no longer depends on the data: when `read` is not one of the configured skip code points (the normal case) no character is ever filtered and every skip character survives into the caller's buffer; when `read` happens to equal a skip code point, the entire just-read block is silently discarded and the method returns 0. The single-character read() override (lines 39-44) correctly tests `filter(ch)`, so the class behaves correctly or not depending on which read API the consumer uses. Subclasses CharacterFilterReader and CharacterSetFilterReader inherit the broken override.

records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled xop:Include/@href is dereferenced as a URL during MTOM attachment resolution (SSRF / local file read)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: CXF attachment resolution treats an XOP/MTOM reference that does not match a supplied attachment as a URL: core `AttachmentUtil.getAttachmentDataSource(String contentId, ...)` falls through to `new URLDataSource(new URL(contentId))` for any value containing "://" that does not start with "cid:", and the Aegis `AttachmentUtil.getAttachment(String id, ...)` falls back to `new URLDataSource(new URL(id))` whenever no attachment matches the href. Neither site restricts the scheme, host, or port, and neither requires the reference to be a local MIME content-id, so `http:`, `https:`, `ftp:`, `file:` and `jar:` URLs supplied in the message are fetched by the server when the attachment stream is read.

CXF attachment resolution treats an XOP/MTOM reference that does not match a supplied attachment as a URL: core `AttachmentUtil.getAttachmentDataSource(String contentId, ...)` falls through to `new URLDataSource(new URL(contentId))` for any value containing "://" that does not start with "cid:", and the Aegis `AttachmentUtil.getAttachment(String id, ...)` falls back to `new URLDataSource(new URL(id))` whenever no attachment matches the href. Neither site restricts the scheme, host, or port, and neither requires the reference to be a local MIME content-id, so `http:`, `https:`, `ftp:`, `file:` and `jar:` URLs supplied in the message are fetched by the server when the attachment stream is read.

records.claim_title: Server-side request forgery via unvalidated OAuth2 `request_uri` (and inverted `client_id` claim check) in JwtRequestCodeFilter
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: JwtRequestCodeFilter.process() accepts security-relevant data straight from the untrusted authorization request. If the `request` parameter is absent, it reads the `request_uri` parameter and, when the value merely starts with `https://` (getPrefix() ignores the `client` argument and returns a constant), it calls WebClient.create(requestUri).get(String.class), causing the CXF server to issue an outbound HTTPS GET to an arbitrary host/port/path chosen by the requester. There is no host/port allow-list, no check against the client's registered URIs, and no restriction to the authorization server's own hosts, despite the TODO in getPrefix noting that hosts should be restricted. In the same method the request-object claim check is inverted: the condition throws when the `client_id` claim equals the authenticated client's id and therefore accepts a request object whose `client_id` claim differs from the authenticated client.

records.claim_title: URIUtils.extractHost accepts malformed/ambiguous authority components and can derive a target host that differs from the host actually used for the request
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: URIUtils.extractHost falls back to ad-hoc string parsing of the raw authority whenever java.net.URI.getHost() returns null (lines 341-376): it strips everything before the FIRST '@' and everything from the FIRST ':' onward (taking only leading digits as port). It then accepts almost any resulting non-blank string as a host (line 379-381). The parser does not validate that the authority is a well-formed server-based authority, does not reject a second '@', embedded brackets/backslashes/percent-escapes or control characters, and silently truncates instead of failing. Because the same raw authority is written to the wire in proxy mode (URIUtils.rewriteURIForRoute leaves absolute request URIs unchanged when using a proxy) and re-parsed independently by the proxy/server, the client-side target/route host and the actual request destination can diverge. ProtocolExec derives the Host/target independently from uri.getHost() (lines 148-155), so for these malformed authorities one code path uses the ad-hoc value while another treats the URI as having no valid host.

records.claim_title: Privilege escalation to AllPermission via wiki-name collision with the Admin group member
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultUserProfile.setFullname() computes the user's wiki name by deleting all whitespace from the user-supplied full name (WHITESPACE = "\\s"). UserManager.setUserProfile() checks uniqueness of the login name, full name and e-mail, but never of the derived wiki name, and findByWikiName() is only used for lookups, never for a duplicate check. At login, AbstractUserDatabase.getPrincipals() injects the wiki name as a WikiPrincipal(WIKI_NAME), and group membership is decided purely by name: GroupManager.isUserInRole() -> Group.isMember() -> Group.findMember() compares only Principal.getName() (WikiPrincipal.equals() is also name-only). WikiSession.injectGroupPrincipals() therefore adds GroupPrincipal("Admin") to a session whose WIKI_NAME principal is "Administrator", and AuthorizationManager.allowedByLocalPolicy() grants that group principal the AllPermission defined for group Admin in the default jspwiki.policy.

records.claim_title: Infinite loop in COSParser.parseXref on a cyclic xref /Prev chain (document-open DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: COSParser.parseXref walks the xref chain with `while (prev > 0)` (COSParser.java:211) and takes each next offset from the attacker-controlled trailer /Prev entry (line 272) or from the xref-stream dictionary (line 287) without recording visited offsets, without an iteration bound, and without an EOF/cycle check. checkXRefOffset() (lines 1165-1187) returns a syntactically valid xref offset unchanged in both lenient and non-lenient modes, so a cycle of two valid xref sections is re-parsed forever. records.claim_title: Crafted PDF page tree causes unbounded recursion / exponential traversal in page-tree walks (DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The page-tree walkers recurse into attacker-controlled /Kids entries without tracking already-visited dictionaries and without any depth or node-count limit. COSParser.checkPagesDictionary (pdfbox/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/pdfparser/COSParser.java:2289-2328) recurses on every kid whose /Type is /Pages (line 2315) and PDPageTree recurses in PageIterator.enqueueKids (pdfbox/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/pdmodel/PDPageTree.java:162-176, recursion line 169), in get(int,COSDictionary,int) (lines 239-298), in findPage (lines 327-345) and in getInheritableAttribute (lines 100-115). A kid array that contains an ancestor (cycle) yields infinite recursion/StackOverflowError, and a kid array that references the same subtree several times yields exponential work (2^depth leaf visits). No visited-set, depth counter, or /Count consistency check exists anywhere in these loops, unlike other hardening elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., the /Prev xref loop set in COSParser.java:314-409, the unknown-direct-object loop guard in BaseParser.java:957-963, or the transparency-group guard in PageDrawer.java:1537-1543).

records.claim_title: StAX signature verification uses attacker-supplied ds:KeyValue instead of the configured signatureVerificationKey
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.setTokenKey only calls token.setPublicKey(configuredKey) when the token type is not KeyValueToken; for a KeyValueToken it falls into the else branch and stores the configured PublicKey via token.setSecretKey("", key). records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled rememberMe cookie reaches native Java deserialization without integrity protection or class allowlisting
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The rememberMe identity is treated as trusted data: CookieRememberMeManager reads the request cookie and Base64-decodes it (no signature/MAC), AbstractRememberMeManager.decrypt() decrypts it with the configured AES key and then passes the plaintext straight to DefaultSerializer.deserialize(), whose ClassResolvingObjectInputStream.readObject() resolves and instantiates any class name present in the stream (ClassUtils.forName, no allowlist/filter). The default cipher service is AES-CBC with PKCS5 padding and no integrity check; JcaCipherService.crypt() wraps decryption/padding failures in CryptoException, so decryption errors are distinguishable from parsing errors (padding-oracle precondition). Consequently, anyone who knows or can recover the cipher key can supply an arbitrary serialized object graph that is deserialized before authentication completes, and can also forge a remembered PrincipalCollection.

records.claim_title: Href validation/sanitization bypassed by HTML named character references (e.g. :) yielding javascript: URLs
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert:
The href path validates a string in which only URL percent-encoding and the five XML predefined entities (amp, lt, gt, quot, apos) plus numeric references have been decoded. `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeXml` (commons-lang3 3.6) does not decode HTML5 named character references such as `:`, `	`, `
`, and the allowed-attribute regex in the policy treats `&` and `;` as ordinary allowed characters (onsiteURL/offsiteURL). The sanitizer never escapes `&` in its output (it only percent-encodes `"`, `'`, `>`, `<`, backtick, space and `:` after a query mark), so the returned value still contains `:`. A browser HTML-parses that attribute value and resolves the entity to `:` after validation, reconstructing a dangerous scheme (e.g. `javascript:`), which the validator had rejected in its decoded form. The sibling `XSSFilterImpl.isValidHref` has the same decoding gap: when `unescapeXml`/`URLDecoder` leave the string unchanged it validates the raw input, which contains no literal `:` and therefore matches the allow-list.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated OGNL expression injection via multipart Content-Type error message (multipart parse error path evaluates attacker-controlled text)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The Jakarta multipart parser embeds the raw request Content-Type value in the error message produced by commons-fileupload 1.3.1 and then feeds that attacker-controlled exception message into the localization machinery as the *default message*: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(..., e.getMessage(), ...). Because no bundle key named 'struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException' exists anywhere in the project (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException keys are defined in struts-messages*.properties), findDefaultText() returns null and the attacker string becomes the message; LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() then calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack), which parses ${...}/%{...} and evaluates them via ValueStack.findValue() using the request's OGNL context/member access. Dispatcher.wrapRequest() gates the multipart path with contentType.contains("multipart/form-data"), so a header that merely *contains* that literal (e.g. inside the injected expression) is routed into the vulnerable parser.

The Jakarta multipart parser embeds the raw request Content-Type value in the error message produced by commons-fileupload 1.3.1 and then feeds that attacker-controlled exception message into the localization machinery as the *default message*: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(..., e.getMessage(), ...). Because no bundle key named 'struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException' exists anywhere in the project (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException keys are defined in struts-messages*.properties), findDefaultText() returns null and the attacker string becomes the message; LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() then calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack), which parses ${...}/%{...} and evaluates them via ValueStack.findValue() using the request's OGNL context/member access. Dispatcher.wrapRequest() gates the multipart path with contentType.contains("multipart/form-data"), so a header that merely *contains* that literal (e.g. inside the injected expression) is routed into the vulnerable parser.

records.claim_title: Class-access exclusion disabled for request-parameter and cookie names, allowing OGNL ClassLoader manipulation
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The class-access exclusion that fixed the earlier S2-020/S2-021 class-loader manipulation was disabled. In xwork-core ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams(), the line that unconditionally added Pattern.compile("(.*\.|^|.*|\[('|"))class(\.|('|")]|\[).*") to excludeParams is commented out (lines 510-511), so parameter names matching the accepted-name whitelist but containing the class chain are not filtered. records.claim_title: OGNL injection via CookieInterceptor cookie names with no Class/ClassLoader access restriction (class-loader manipulation)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Two controls combine into a gap. (1) CookieInterceptor validates cookie names only against the character whitelist ACCEPTED_PATTERN = "[a-zA-Z0-9\\.\\]\\[_'\\s]+", then passes the raw cookie name to ValueStack.setValue(name, value), which compiles and evaluates it as an OGNL expression; the framework's CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN/ExcludedPatterns blacklist is explicitly not applied (the intended check is commented out at CookieInterceptor.java:248). (2) SecurityMemberAccess.isAccessible (the OGNL MemberAccess used by the value stack) only enforces static-method rules and property-name accept/exclude sets; it has no excludedClasses/excludedPackageNames style target-class restriction, and the default value stack created in OgnlValueStack.setRoot installs it with empty accept/exclude sets. Therefore a dotted chain that reaches java.lang.Class/java.lang.ClassLoader (e.g. class.classLoader.resources... ) is not rejected: the property names 'class'/'classLoader' individually do not match the blacklist regex (it requires the token 'class' followed by '.', quote, '[' or ']'), and no target-class check exists.

records.claim_title: Attacker-influenced multipart error message is evaluated as OGNL (Content-Type header -> expression injection in default request pipeline)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse() catches every parse failure and builds the user-visible error with buildErrorMessage(), which passes e.getMessage() as the defaultMessage argument of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(). Commons FileUpload exception messages for malformed multipart requests embed the raw, attacker-supplied Content-Type/boundary text. LocalizedTextUtil.findText() finds no bundle entry for the synthesized key (struts-messages*.properties only define SizeLimitExceededException/IOException), so it falls through to getDefaultMessage(), which calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) on that default message (LocalizedTextUtil.java:663). translateVariables extracts %{...}/${...} bodies and evaluates them via stack.findValue() (TextParseUtil.java:153-168), i.e. full OGNL against the request's ValueStack. No interceptor/action has executed yet at this point, so the ParametersInterceptor's ReflectionContextState DENY_METHOD_EXECUTION / CREATE_NULL_OBJECTS guards are not set, and the stack's SecurityMemberAccess (default allowStaticMethodAccess=false, default.properties:202) only blocks static *methods*, not static field reads - the classic member-access reset used in OGNL injection chains. The gate is permissive: Dispatcher.wrapRequest only requires the header to *contain* 'multipart/form-data' anywhere (Dispatcher.java:800), while the parser rejects values that do not *start* with 'multipart/', so the header can carry both the trigger string and the expression.

records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled DMI method name is evaluated as OGNL (OGNL injection / possible RCE when Dynamic Method Invocation is enabled)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultActionMapper stores the raw, unsanitized method: parameter value (and the text after an exclamation mark in the action name) into ActionMapping.method (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/mapper/DefaultActionMapper.java:136-142 and 269-284). DefaultActionProxy.resolveMethod copies it into proxy.method and validates it only with ActionConfig.isAllowedMethod (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/DefaultActionProxy.java:163-192). records.claim_title: Self-service SCIM update of a user's own record allows changing security-sensitive attributes (origin, active, verified, externalId, username, email)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The `/Users/**` filter chain authorizes PUT/PATCH for the caller's own user with `@self.isUserSelf(request,1)` only; no field-level restriction is applied. `ScimUserEndpoints.updateUser`/`patchUser` pass the caller-supplied object to `JdbcScimUserProvisioning.update`, whose SQL writes `origin`, `verified`, `externalId`, `userName`, `email`, `active` (and salt). The codebase contains an unused guard, `ScimUserSelfUpdateAllowed.isAllowed(request)`, which compares the database record against the request body and returns false when email, username, verified, active or origin differ - exactly the missing check. Additionally `ScimUser.patch()` copies `active`/`verified` unconditionally from a patch object whose primitive defaults are both `true`, so even a PATCH body that omits those fields forces them to true. `ScimUserEndpoints.updateUser` also calls `checkIsEditAllowed(user.getOrigin(), request)` with the attacker-supplied body origin rather than the stored origin, so the disable-internal-user-management guard is evaluated against attacker-chosen data.

records.claim_title: Untrusted ESI markup can force the proxy to fetch and execute an arbitrary remote XSLT stylesheet (SSRF and possible remote code execution)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: ESI directives come from the provider (backend) response body and are treated as trusted without any validation of the URLs they reference and without sandboxing of the transformation engine. In `IncludeElement.processPage` the `stylesheet` attribute is read verbatim from the parsed tag and passed to `new XsltRenderer(xslt, driver, httpRequest)` (core and parallelesi). `XsltRenderer` retrieves that URI with `driver.render(template, ...)`; `ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString` only prefixes the configured base URL when the value does NOT already start with `http://`/`https://`, so an absolute attacker URL is used as-is, and `DriverRequest` marks such URLs `external`, causing `HttpClientRequestExecutor.createOutgoingRequest` to *skip* host rewriting and connect to the attacker-chosen host. The same constructor also honours attacker-supplied `xpath`; the aggregator `<!--$includeblock$...$-->` path has the same absolute-URL behaviour via `ElementAttributesFactory`.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In XmlFactory's constructor, the default XMLInputFactory is only hardened for external entity expansion: xmlIn.setProperty(XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, Boolean.FALSE) (lines 112-116, with comment referencing dataformat-xml#190). records.ground_truth_vulnerability: HtmlSessionInformationsReport writes session remoteAddr containing X-Forwarded-For without HTML escaping

records.claim_title: Reflected/stored XSS in the monitoring HTML reports via contextually incorrect output encoding of attacker-controlled values
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The report layer relies on encoding helpers that are not safe for the context in which they are used. I18N.urlEncode() (I18N.java:142-144) only calls javascriptEncode(), which prepends backslashes before \\, \n, \" and ' but leaves the raw quote characters, spaces and tabs in the output; it is then used to build single-quoted HTML attributes (href/value/src). I18N.htmlEncode() (I18N.java:152-160) escapes &, <, > and newline but not quote characters, so it is also unsafe inside attributes. In addition, a few values derived directly from the request are written with no encoding at all: anchorNameForRedirect (the `counter` request parameter, via Action.getContextName()) is concatenated into a single-quoted JavaScript string in HtmlCoreReport.writeMessageIfNotNull (HtmlCoreReport.java:309-313), and the session's remoteAddr - built from the attacker-controlled X-Forwarded-For header in MonitoringFilter.putUserInfoInSession (MonitoringFilter.java:313-323) - is written raw into the sessions table (HtmlSessionInformationsReport.java:158-163). An attacker-supplied value containing a quote plus a whitespace character (e.g. %20/%09) and an event-handler attribute therefore terminates the attribute/string context and injects markup or script that the victim's browser executes in the monitoring origin.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Sventon.DescriptorImpl.doCheckUrl and Sventon2.DescriptorImpl.doCheckUrl are Stapler form-validation methods that take the fully attacker-controlled `value` query parameter, append a slash, construct `new URL(v)` and fetch it from the Jenkins controller (URLCheck.open / findText). The only gate is `project == null && !ADMINISTER || project != null && !project.hasPermission(Item.EXTENDED_READ)`. There is also no URL scheme/format restriction in Sventon (unlike FishEyeSVN's URL_PATTERN check), so any scheme the JVM URL/URLConnection stack supports is accepted.

records.claim_title: DOM scanner validates only the first child of <style>, leaving sibling CSS nodes unfiltered
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In AntiSamyDOMScanner.actionValidate(), a <style> element with a matching policy rule is handed to processStyleTag() before any content traversal. processStyleTag() takes only ele.getFirstChild(), runs CssScanner.scanStyleSheet() on that single node and then overwrites that same node (firstChild.setNodeValue(cleanHTML) or "/* */"). It never iterates over ele.getChildNodes(), so any additional text/CDATA siblings are never CSS-scanned. Later, processChildren() -> recursiveValidateTag() only handles Element nodes (two special cases: comment and CDATA conversion) and returns early for non-element nodes ('if (!isElement) return;'), so the remaining text siblings are simply passed through to the serializer. The DOM parser is explicitly configured for CDATA sections ('http://cyberneko.org/html/features/scanner/cdata-sections' = true and 'scanner/style/strip-cdata-delims' = false), so a <style> body containing a <![CDATA[...]]> section can be represented as more than one child node, e.g. a CDATASection plus a trailing text node, and only the first one is validated.

records.claim_title: XXE in apoc.load.xml / apoc.load.xmlSimple / apoc.xml.import: local file disclosure and SSRF bypassing apoc.import.file.enabled
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The XML parsers used by the XML loading/import procedures are instantiated without disabling DTDs or external entities. In Xml.xmlXpathToMapResult (src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java:65-68) a DocumentBuilderFactory is created with only namespaceAware/ignoringElementContentWhitespace set and is then used at line 74 to parse bytes fetched from the caller-supplied URL (Util.openInputStream). The shared StAX factory (src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java:39) used by getXMLStreamReaderFromUrl (lines 121-125, called from apoc.load.xmlSimple line 107-109 and apoc.xml.import line 397-399) only sets javax.xml.stream.isCoalescing and leaves SUPPORT_DTD/isSupportingExternalEntities permissive. XmlGraphMLReader.parseXML (src/main/java/apoc/export/graphml/XmlGraphMLReader.java:179-183), used by apoc.import.graphml, is the same pattern. Repository-wide searches found no setFeature, XMLConstants, disallow-doctype-decl, external-general-entities=false, ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD, expandEntityReferences, or FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING anywhere, so no mitigation exists in this code. FileUtils.checkReadAllowed (src/main/java/apoc/util/FileUtils.java:137-140) only evaluates the outer URL string; entities resolved inside the document are never checked, so the apoc.import.file.enabled gate is not enforced for them.

records.claim_title: Zip Slip path traversal (arbitrary file write) in neo4j-admin load archive extraction
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Loader.extract loop trusts archive entry names. In `loadEntry`, `Path file = destination.resolve(entry.getName())` is used directly for `Files.createDirectories(file)` and `Files.newOutputStream(file)` with no `normalize()` and no containment check that the result stays under `destination`. `determineEntryDestination` only looks at `Paths.get(entry.getName()).getFileName()` to choose between the database and transaction-log directories, so it does not constrain the full path used for extraction. Nothing in the Loader (or its helpers `Utils`, `IncorrectFormat`) sanitizes, rejects, or re-roots entry names, even though a containment helper (`Util.isSameOrChildPath`) exists elsewhere in the command-line module.

records.claim_title: ONOS application REST endpoints (RESTCONF server, VTN web, and other WABs) are deployed without authentication
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Multiple ONOS web-application bundles (WABs) declare a JAX-RS ServletContainer mapped to /* but their WEB-INF/web.xml contains no active <security-constraint>/<auth-constraint> (role admin, BASIC realm karaf), unlike sibling WABs such as web/api, acl, dhcp and segmentrouting. Under Pax-Web/Karaf the per-WAB web.xml is the only authentication mechanism, so JAX-RS resources of an unconstrained WAB are served without any JAAS login. In apps/vtn/vtnweb/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml the constraint block exists but is commented out (lines 23-42) with the literal comment 'TODO: this should be uncommented', and in protocols/restconf/server/rpp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml the constraint is absent altogether.

records.claim_title: Path traversal (Tar Slip) in project archive import allows arbitrary file write outside the workspace
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: FileProjectManager.untar() trusts tar entry names from an untrusted archive: it does `File destEntry = new File(destDir, tarEntry.getName())`, creates parent directories and writes the entry contents with `new FileOutputStream(destEntry)` without normalizing the resulting path or verifying it remains inside `destDir`. The equivalent hardening exists elsewhere in the codebase (`ImportingUtilities.allocateFile()` normalizes with `toPath().normalize()` and rejects names that escape the archive root, with the comment 'For CVE-2018-19859, issue #1840'), but this project-import path was not covered by that guard, so a `../` entry (e.g. `../../../../home/user/.bashrc`) escapes the project directory.

records.claim_title: XXE in XML importer: StAX parser resolves external entities during import/preview
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XmlImporter.createXMLStreamReader (main/src/com/google/refine/importers/XmlImporter.java:322-328) builds the parser with XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and sets only XMLInputFactory.IS_COALESCING=true and XMLInputFactory.IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES=true. It never disables DTD support (XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false), never disables external entity resolution (XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false), and sets no accessExternalDTD/accessExternalSchema restriction. In the default JDK (the app targets JDK 8) supportDTD and isSupportingExternalEntities default to true, so attacker-supplied DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations are processed and external general entities are fetched and substituted (entity replacement is explicitly enabled). The same factory is used both for parser-UI preview (createParserUIInitializationData, line 91) and for full import via the XmlParser TreeReader (lines 214-219, parseOneFile lines 196-212), so merely previewing an uploaded XML file triggers resolution server-side.

records.claim_title: XXE via JAXB unmarshalling without SecureUnmarshaller in Atom and XOP providers
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RESTEasy's central mitigation for XXE in JAXB providers is `SecureUnmarshaller`, which wraps the JAXB Unmarshaller and forces external-general-entities/external-parameter-entities=false, disallow-doctype-decl=true (default) and FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING=true. The Atom providers and the XOP JAXB helper bypass this wrapper and unmarshal the raw request body directly with `JAXBContext.createUnmarshaller()`, so the project's secure-by-default JAXB parsing contract is not applied on these paths.

records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled request parameter names parsed and evaluated as SpEL in MapDataBinder property binding
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MapDataBinder's MapPropertyAccessor turns each incoming request parameter name into a SpEL expression: `Expression expression = PARSER.parseExpression(propertyName); expression.setValue(context, value);` (MapDataBinder.java:187-190). records.claim_title: Remote SpEL injection via STOMP subscription `selector` header in DefaultSubscriptionRegistry
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultSubscriptionRegistry treats the client-controlled STOMP native header `selector` as a Spring EL expression: addSubscriptionInternal() parses it with a default SpelExpressionParser (line 147, expressionParser field line 76) and filterSubscriptions() later evaluates it with `new StandardEvaluationContext(message)` (line 212) and `expression.getValue(context, boolean.class)` (line 216). StandardEvaluationContext uses the default SpEL type locator/method resolvers, so expressions can reference types such as java.lang.Runtime and invoke static methods/constructors. There is no allow-list, no SimpleEvaluationContext, and no sanitization of the selector text; only parse/evaluation exceptions are caught and logged.

records.claim_title: Unbounded HTTP Range header is expanded into one response part per range (no coalescing/cap), enabling amplification DoS when serving resources
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The framework accepts an unbounded list of byte ranges from the request header and converts it 1:1 into ResourceRegion objects without merging overlapping/adjacent ranges or imposing any cap, then streams every region separately. HttpRange.parseRanges (spring-web/.../HttpRange.java:127-142) splits the attacker-supplied 'Range' value into as many tokens as fit in the header, and HttpRange.toResourceRegions (:174-183) creates one ResourceRegion per range with the requested length (a 'start-' or suffix range yields the full resource length). ResourceRegion (spring-core/.../ResourceRegion.java:29-77) has no merge/coalesce support. ResourceRegionHttpMessageConverter.writeResourceRegionCollection (spring-web/.../ResourceRegionHttpMessageConverter.java:171-215) then writes each region in full, opening a fresh InputStream and calling StreamUtils.copyRange per range, so the body length equals the SUM of requested range lengths rather than the size of their union.

records.claim_title: RegexRequestMatcher compiles patterns without DOTALL, allowing authorization-rule bypass via newline in the decoded request path
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RegexRequestMatcher builds its Pattern with Pattern.compile(pattern) (or Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE only) and then evaluates pattern.matcher(url).matches() against servletPath + pathInfo. Because Pattern.DOTALL is not set, the dot does not match line terminators. A URL whose decoded path contains a newline (for example a %0a encoded into the path) therefore fails to match a rule whose regex uses a dot (canonical example /admin/.*), even though the same request can still be dispatched by the application routing layer (Ant/PathPattern '**' matching tolerates the extra character in the last segment). The restricted authorization rule is skipped and the next matching rule (commonly anyRequest().permitAll() or a weaker rule) decides the request, producing an authorization bypass. The code is the pre-fix version of the upstream flaw later assigned CVE-2022-22978.

records.claim_title: SpEL expression injection in whitelabel OAuth2 approval page via attacker-influenced scope names (potential RCE)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint.createScopes() builds the approval-page HTML by substituting the keys of the model's "scopes" map (which are scope names, prefixed with "scope.") verbatim into the %scope% and %key% markers of the SCOPE template fragment (WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint.java:46-60). The assembled template is then passed to SpelView, whose constructor installs a PropertyPlaceholderHelper with prefix "${" and suffix "}" and a resolver that calls new SpelExpressionParser().parseExpression(name).getValue(context) (SpelView.java:47-57); render() runs the resolver over the whole template (SpelView.java:64-74). records.ground_truth_vulnerability: Retrofit RequestBuilder.addPathParam permits complete dot/dot-dot path segments
records.ground_truth: Retrofit RequestBuilder.addPathParam permits complete dot/dot-dot path segments
records.claim_title: Path traversal in `@Path` parameter substitution (dot segments survive URL normalization)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `RequestBuilder.addPathParam` substitutes the converted `@Path` value into `relativeUrl` using `canonicalizeForPath`, which only percent-encodes control chars, `"<>^`{}|\?#`, and (when `encoded=false`) `/` and `%`. The `.` character is never encoded or rejected, so a value of `.` or `..` produces a literal relative-path dot segment. `RequestBuilder.get()` (and the query-parameter path in `addQueryParam`) then resolves that relative URL against the configured base URL through OkHttp's `HttpUrl.resolve`/`HttpUrl.newBuilder`, which applies RFC 3986 remove_dot_segments normalization; the dot segment is therefore consumed during resolution and the preceding path segment is popped instead of being sent literally. `RequestFactory.validatePathName` validates only the annotation placeholder name (`[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*` and presence in the template), never the runtime value. The mitigation intent (keep an untrusted value inside one path segment) is visible in the code (`/` and `%` are encoded), but the dot-segment normalization path is not covered.

records.ground_truth_vulnerability: XStream clears insecureWarning before InternalBlackList converter checks, disabling default gadget blacklist
records.ground_truth: XStream clears insecureWarning before InternalBlackList converter checks, disabling default gadget blacklist
records.claim_title: Default XStream configuration deserializes arbitrary attacker-specified types: internal blacklist is disabled during unmarshalling
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XStream's built-in protection for a default (uninitialized-security) instance is self-defeating. (1) setupSecurity() registers AnyTypePermission.ANY for every new XStream instance and only raises the insecureWarning flag (XStream.java:693-700). (2) SecurityMapper.realClass then returns any class resolved from element names/class attributes (SecurityMapper.java:70-78), because AnyTypePermission.allows always returns true (AnyTypePermission.java:21-23). (3) The converter that is supposed to block the known exploit types, InternalBlackList, only reports those types when insecureWarning is true (XStream.java:2539-2546), but XStream.unmarshal() sets insecureWarning=false at the start of the call, before the marshalling strategy performs any conversion or converter lookup (XStream.java:1480-1485). Consequently the EventHandler/$LazyIterator/javax.crypto.* block is never in effect while parsing untrusted input, and ReflectionConverter (registered at PRIORITY_VERY_LOW, XStream.java:958-959) instantiates the attacker-chosen type. The same flag also drives the 'framework not initialized' warning, so gating a security control on it is logically wrong.

records.claim_title: Unchecked Content-Length integer overflow in HttpTransferEncoding.parsePositiveLong allows HTTP/1.1 body-length desynchronization (request-smuggling primitive)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: HttpTransferEncoding.parsePositiveLong() accumulates value += digit * multiplier; multiplier *= 10 in a long with no overflow/range check. A decimal Content-Length longer than 19 digits silently wraps modulo 2^64 instead of throwing, so the parsed length can be 0 or an arbitrary small value (e.g. a value that is a multiple of 2^64 parses as 0). The request path then either calls Connectors.terminateRequest (treating the request as having no body) or installs a FixedLengthStreamSourceConduit with the wrapped length, while the bytes the peer considers to be the body remain on the connection and are parsed as a subsequent pipelined request. No earlier stage validates the numeric value: Connectors.areRequestHeadersValid() only rejects TE+CL and duplicate TE/CL headers, not oversized values, and the HTTP header parser accepts any run of digits.

records.claim_title: SecureObjectInputStream package whitelist can be bypassed because isSubpackage() uses startsWith() without a package boundary
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SecureObjectInputStream.resolveClass() (line 54) allows a class if classesWhitelist.contains(className) or isSubpackage(className). isSubpackage() (lines 60-68) computes FilenameUtils.removeExtension(className) — i.e., treats the class name as a filename and strips everything after the last '.' — and then accepts the class when any configured package string satisfies packageName.startsWith(pack). There is no requirement that the prefix be followed by '.' (no package boundary), so any class whose package name merely shares a leading string with a whitelisted package is accepted. Example: whitelisting package 'org.apache.commons.collections' also admits 'org.apache.commons.collections4.functors.InvokerTransformer' (and any other prefix-sharing package such as 'com.app' admitting 'com.appEvil.Gadget'), even though the operator's intent was a different artifact/package. Sorting/formatting the class name as a file path additionally mangles names (e.g., inner-class and array descriptors), further weakening the check. The javadoc only claims subpackages are intentionally admitted; prefix-sharing sibling packages are not intended.

records.claim_title: SAX filter misidentifies style elements via endsWith instead of equality, routing other validate-action tags' content through the CSS path
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MagicSAXFilter.startElement computes `boolean isStyle = "style".endsWith(element.localpart);`. String.endsWith on the literal "style" returns true not only for the actual `<style>` element but for any element name that is a suffix of "style" (e.g. "e", "le", "tyle"). The branch is gated only by `tag.isAction("validate")` and the policy tag lookup, not by an exact name match or `policy.getStyleTag()`. The DOM counterpart uses the safe form `"style".equals(tagNameLowerCase) && policy.getStyleTag() != null` (AntiSamyDOMScanner.java:357), showing the intended check.

records.claim_title: Local-URL restriction in policy loading is applied to the base URL only, so resolved include/systemId URLs (http/https/file) are opened without verification
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Policy.verifyLocalUrl(URL) (Policy.java 1053-1062) enforces that only file:/jar: URLs are used, but the two call sites verify only the *base* URL: getDocumentElementByUrl calls verifyLocalUrl(baseUrl) at line 576 and resolveEntity calls it at line 1019, then each resolves an attacker-influenceable href/systemId against that base with `new URL(baseUrl, href)` and opens the stream directly (url.openStream() at lines 584 and 1025) without ever calling verifyLocalUrl on the resolved URL. An absolute href/systemId therefore overrides the base and can reach any scheme/host (for example http://169.254.169.254/..., http://internal/, or file:///etc/passwd). The fallback paths (lines 586-597 and 1028-1038, via URIUtils.resolveAsString) likewise construct and open a URL with no protocol/host check. This contradicts the class documentation and SpotBugs suppressions, which assert that only local file/jar URLs are allowed (Policy.java 318-325, 400-401, 532-533, 565-566, 1009-1010).

records.claim_title: Windows child processes inherit named-pipe handles of other NuProcess children (cross-process stdio exposure)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: WindowsProcess.createPipes() builds one SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES with bInheritHandle=true and lpSecurityDescriptor=null and applies it to the server end of all three named pipes (stdout, stderr, stdin), and prepareProcess() then calls CreateProcessW with bInheritHandles=true. Because every NuProcess child is started with bInheritHandles=true, each new child receives duplicates of all currently open inheritable handles in the JVM, including the stdin/stderr/stdout pipe server handles created for other NuProcess instances that are still running (all of which are marked inheritable for the lifetime of the process). Nothing constrains inheritance to the specific per-child handle triplet (e.g. no PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_LIST).

records.claim_title: Unvalidated `redirectedFrom` parameter allows open redirect in AppointmentBlockFormController
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In the POST handler `onSubmit`, the request parameter `redirectedFrom` is bound with `@RequestParam(required = false)` and used directly to build the view name: `return "redirect:" + redirectedFrom;` (line 313). There is no whitelist/format validation and the concatenation happens outside the `if (Context.isAuthenticated())` block, so the value fully controls the redirect target. The GET handler in the same controller (lines 79-95) shows the intended behaviour: it only treats the parameter as meaningful when `redirectedFrom.equals("appointmentBlockCalendar.list")`, i.e. the value is expected to be one of a few fixed internal page names; all other redirects in the module are static strings (e.g. AppointmentBlockListController line 160/165, AppointmentBlockCalendarController lines 163/167/171).

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated remote config update applies arbitrary properties to internal config objects, enabling OS command execution on the broker and arbitrary file write on the name server
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Neither update-config endpoint validates the keys or values it accepts. AdminBrokerProcessor.updateBrokerConfig (RequestCode.UPDATE_BROKER_CONFIG) and DefaultRequestProcessor.updateConfig (RequestCode.UPDATE_NAMESRV_CONFIG) parse the request body with MixAll.string2Properties and pass the result to Configuration.update(), which calls MixAll.properties2Object(properties, configObject) for every registered config object. properties2Object reflectively invokes any setter whose lower-camel-case name matches a property key, so security-critical operational fields are remotely settable: BrokerConfig.setRocketmqHome(String), BrokerConfig.setFilterServerNums(int), BrokerConfig.setNamesrvAddr(String), NamesrvConfig.setConfigStorePath(String). There is no allowlist, no sensitive-key rejection, and no authentication requirement on either endpoint (broker ACL is off by default and the name server has no ACL implementation). Broker: FilterServerManager.createFilterServer() builds the string "sh <rocketmqHome>/bin/startfsrv.sh <config>" (or a Windows equivalent), and FilterServerUtil.callShell splits it on spaces and runs it through Runtime.getRuntime().exec; attacker-controlled rocketmqHome/namesrvAddr are concatenated directly into that command line, and filterServerNums controls periodic execution, so injection into the sh argument vector yields OS command execution. Name server: Configuration.getStorePath() reads NamesrvConfig.configStorePath (set via setStorePathFromConfig in NamesrvController), and Configuration.update() unconditionally calls persist() -> MixAll.string2File(allConfigs, storePath), so changing configStorePath in the same request makes the name server write its config content to an attacker-chosen path (parent directories are created).

records.claim_title: Kubernetes-backed credential is retained (revocation not enforced) when a MODIFIED secret fails conversion
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: KubernetesCredentialProvider.eventReceived handles MODIFIED exclusively by calling addSecret(secret) (lines 255-259). addSecret only performs map.put when convertSecret returns a non-null credential (lines 239-244). convertSecret returns null, without touching the existing map entry, when the type label has no registered SecretToCredentialConverter (lines 293-294 and 308-309) or when the converter raises CredentialsConvertionException (lines 295-306). There is no else-branch that removes the previously converted credential for that secret ID, so the in-memory credentials map keeps serving the old credential object (with the old secret value) after the Kubernetes secret has been edited into an unconvertible state.

records.claim_title: Inverted Class.isAssignableFrom in CheckProfileTypeAuthorizer allows profile-type authorization bypass
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `CheckProfileTypeAuthorizer.check(...)` returns `profile.getClass().isAssignableFrom(element)` instead of `element.isAssignableFrom(profile.getClass())`. The method therefore authorizes a profile only when the profile's actual class is a *superclass* of the class required by configuration (or is exactly equal), which is the opposite of the documented semantics ("checks the current profile type of the authenticated user", documentation/docs/authorizers/profile-authorizers.md:34) and of the idiom used elsewhere in the codebase (Clients.java:144, AbstractAttributeConverter.java:23). Because `AbstractRequireAnyAuthorizer.isProfileAuthorized`/`AbstractRequireElementAuthorizer.isAuthorized` and `DefaultAuthorizationChecker.isAuthorized` treat `true` as authorized, a broader profile type satisfies a narrower requirement.

records.claim_title: TemporaryFolder creates test directories with default (world-readable) permissions in the shared temp directory
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: TemporaryFolder#createTemporaryFolderIn() (src/main/java/org/junit/rules/TemporaryFolder.java:232-251) gets an unpredictable name via File.createTempFile(junit, .tmp, parentFolder) in the system temp directory, deletes the placeholder file, then creates the directory with createdFolder.mkdir() (line 242) and returns it. No permissions are restricted before or after (there is no setReadable/setWritable/setExecutable, PosixFilePermissions or Files.createTempDirectory call anywhere in the tree; searches for these APIs return zero matches). File.mkdir() creates the directory with the process-default mode (0777 & ~umask; typically 0755 with umask 022), so group/other users get read+execute on it. Files created through newFile(String) use File.createNewFile() (lines 153-160) and directories through newFolder(...)/mkdirs() (lines 184-223), also inheriting default permissions, so the contents are readable as well.

records.claim_title: Default XStream security setup allows arbitrary attacker-named types to be instantiated during XML unmarshalling (incomplete denylist) leading to deserialization gadget code execution
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `XStream.setupSecurity()` installs the permissive `AnyTypePermission.ANY` and only denies `java.beans.EventHandler`, class names matching `.*\$LazyIterator`, and `javax.crypto.*` (XStream.java:639-649). `SecurityMapper.realClass()` (mapper/SecurityMapper.java:64-78) is the only gate between XML-supplied class names and the converter/reflection machinery, and because the ANY permission is evaluated after the few NoPermission denials, practically every class on the classpath is accepted. Converters then instantiate it (`AbstractReflectionConverter.instantiateNewInstance`, lines 569-582; `unmarshal`, lines 274-279) with field population, `readResolve` invocation, and - through `SerializableConverter.doUnmarshal` lines 428-444 - execution of the chosen class's own `readObject(ObjectInputStream)`. The repo itself documents the resulting exposure (`security.html` lines 52-76; `changes.html` lines 31-37 state the upcoming release addresses 'an arbitrary execution of commands when unmarshalling for XStream instances with uninitialized security framework') and `XStream.unmarshal` (lines 1396-1404) only prints a warning ('using predefined black list on your own risk') instead of enforcing a safe default.

records.claim_title: Remote SpEL/expression injection via the 'spring.cloud.function.routing-expression' message header in RoutingFunction
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RoutingFunction treats the value of the message header `spring.cloud.function.routing-expression` as a trusted SpEL expression. `route(...)` reads the header verbatim (line 125-126) and `functionFromExpression(...)` calls `spelParser.parseExpression(routingExpression)` then `expression.getValue(this.evalContext, input, String.class)` (lines 208-210) on a `StandardEvaluationContext` (`evalContext`, line 60) configured with `MapAccessor` (line 79) and a bean resolver set from a `BeanFactoryResolver` (lines 80, 146). SpEL with a standard evaluation context supports type references and method invocation, so the routing value is not just a function name but arbitrary executable expression text.

records.claim_title: Filter XML parameter type is attacker-controlled and XStream-deserialized without a type allow-list (XStream 1.4.17)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `DefaultXMLParser.unserializeParameter` trusts the `t` attribute of a parameter element and calls `Class.forName(typeString, true, Thread.currentThread().getContextClassLoader())` on it, then passes the attacker-chosen class to `XStreamParameterManager.unSerialize`, which unmarshals the XML with `NoWarningXStream` (a plain XStream whose only security layer is XStream 1.4.17's version-dependent denylist). records.claim_title: Unbounded recursive wrapper-array unwrapping in StdDeserializer primitive-value helpers -> StackOverflowError DoS
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Non-primitive value types unwrap single-element arrays through StdDeserializer._deserializeFromArray(), which delegates to StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue() (lines 347-369) where a nested START_ARRAY is explicitly rejected ("nested Arrays not allowed with UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS"), and BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray() contains an explicit deeply-nested-array guard (BeanDeserializer.java:631-640, comment dated 23-Aug-2022). The primitive-value parse helpers bypass both: when the current token is START_ARRAY and UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled they call p.nextToken() and then immediately re-invoke themselves, without checking whether the element token is again START_ARRAY: _parseBooleanPrimitive (StdDeserializer.java:413-420), _parseBytePrimitive (582-589), _parseShortPrimitive (652-659), _parseIntPrimitive (720-726), _parseLongPrimitive (871-877), _parseFloatPrimitive (1004-1010), _parseDoublePrimitive (1133-1139), and _parseDateFromArray/_parseDate for java.util.Date (1288-1289, 1298-1322). Each nesting level adds one Java stack frame, so an attacker-chosen nesting depth exhausts the thread stack; _verifyEndArrayForSingle (2112) runs only after the recursive call returns and therefore cannot bound the recursion.

records.claim_title: Unbounded recursion / StackOverflowError when unwrapping deeply nested JSON arrays for bean types (UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray()` (and the near-identical `BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray()`) override the base unwrapping logic but, in the `unwrap` branch, call `deserialize(p, ctxt)` directly on the first array element instead of using `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue()`, which contains the explicit nested-array guard ("nested Arrays not allowed with DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS", StdDeserializer.java lines 355-368). records.ground_truth_vulnerability: BCEL ConstantPoolGen exceeds JVM constant-pool limit and dump truncates the count
records.ground_truth: BCEL ConstantPoolGen exceeds JVM constant-pool limit and dump truncates the count
records.claim_title: Constant pool can grow past the JVM's 65535-entry limit and its count/indexes are silently truncated when written
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `org.apache.bcel.generic.ConstantPoolGen` enforces no maximum constant-pool size: the `ConstantPool(Constant[])`-style constructor at ConstantPoolGen.java:109-118 sets `size = Math.max(256, cs.length + 64)` (already >65535 when `cs.length` is a maximal parsed pool, e.g. 65535), and `adjustSize()` (ConstantPoolGen.java:560-570) grows `size` by repeated doubling with no upper-bound check. `Const.MAX_CP_ENTRIES` (Const.java:640-646) exists but is used nowhere in the repository, indicating the limit check is absent. `getFinalConstantPool()` (ConstantPoolGen.java:590-594) copies all `index` entries into a `ConstantPool`, and `ConstantPool.dump()` (ConstantPool.java:232-239) writes the count with `file.writeShort(constantPool.length)`, which truncates any value >65535 modulo 65536; constant-pool indexes embedded in instructions/attributes are likewise written as 16-bit values. The result is a re-emitted class file whose constant-pool count and indexes do not describe the bytecode the tool saw.

records.claim_title: Unsafe Java deserialization of HTTP request bodies in the EJB-over-HTTP remoting endpoint (__ejb-invoker)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The payara EJB-over-HTTP feature accepts Java-serialized request bodies and deserializes them with a plain ObjectInputStream/ClassLoaderObjectInputStream and no class filtering, whitelist or JEP-290 ObjectInputFilter. In addition, the invoker application carries no declarative security constraint (the endpoint app's web.xml defines only login/error JSPs), and security is only applied programmatically when the invoker's `security-enabled` option is true, whose default is `false`. Consequently, once the invoker application is enabled, the serialized body is processed before any authentication/authorization decision, so an attacker who can reach the HTTP listener fully controls the bytes passed to readObject() and, through deserialization gadget behavior available on the server classpath, can influence server-side execution rather than only the intended EJB invocation.

records.claim_title: NiFi Registry: client-supplied flow identifier used as filesystem path allows path traversal (write/read/delete outside flow storage)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: StandardServiceFacade.createFlow deliberately accepts a client-supplied flow identifier for backwards compatibility with NiFi (identifier is only generated when null; the existing comment notes the identifier check was removed). BucketItem.identifier is only @NotBlank-validated, so values containing path separators and '..' pass validation and are stored in the DB by RegistryService.createFlow/FlowMappings. RegistryService.createFlowSnapshot then builds a StandardFlowSnapshotContext whose flowId is that identifier, and FileSystemFlowPersistenceProvider (the default provider in conf/providers.xml) concatenates bucketId/flowId/version directly into java.io.File paths without normalization or containment verification.

records.claim_title: DirectoryArchiver writes archive-controlled entry names and symlinks outside the destination directory
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DirectoryArchiver.execute() takes ArchiveEntry.getName() from an archive-backed resource collection and builds the output path as destDirectory.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator + fileName, then passes it to copyFile() or SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(). No canonical-path containment check, no rejection of '..' path elements, and no NOFOLLOW handling is applied to the final output path. Consequently archive entry names can traverse above the destination, and an archive-created symlink can redirect later writes.

records.claim_title: SSRF and arbitrary local file read through client-supplied CSVDataSetDef (fileURL/filePath)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The remote data-set lookup API accepts a caller-supplied DataSetDef and resolves/executes it server-side without verifying that the definition was registered or that its data source is within an allowed location/scheme. For CSV data sets the provider passes the definition straight to CSVParser, which opens dataSetDef.getFileURL() with new URL(url).openStream() (no scheme restriction, so file:, http:, ftp:, jar: are all attempted) or falls back to new FileInputStream(new File(dataSetDef.getFilePath())) for any absolute server path. The only CSV validation constraints are @NotNull/@Size (CSVDataSetDef.java lines 29-34) and they are not invoked on the lookup path.

records.claim_title: Unescaped stored role pattern inserted into HTML via innerHTML on role management page (stored/DOM XSS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: src/main/webapp/js/tableManage.js builds markup by string concatenation with innerHTML and interpolates the stored role pattern into a double-quoted attribute without HTML-escaping. In endPatternInput (line 89) the pattern is escaped only for the anchor text ('"' + pattern.escapeHTML() + '"') but is appended raw into the hidden input: name="[pattern]" value="' + pattern + '". The same raw interpolation occurs in the pencil-icon click handler (line 66): '... value="' + inputNode.childNodes[1].value + '"'. A pattern containing a double quote breaks out of the value attribute and injects arbitrary markup/event handlers, which are then parsed and executed by the admin's browser when the pattern edit control is activated/rendered. The helper escapeHTML/doubleEscapeHTML exists in src/main/webapp/js/table.js (lines 70-89) and is used elsewhere in the same file (e.g. line 176/179/186), showing the escaping was intended but omitted at these sinks.

records.claim_title: Netflux realtime channel keys and history-keeper/user identifiers generated with java.util.Random (predictable bearer tokens)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Utils.getRandomHexString(int) creates a fresh java.util.Random (48-bit LCG, not a CSPRNG) per call and appends Integer.toHexString(random.nextInt()) until the requested length is reached (Utils.java lines 40-48). It mints security-relevant values: Channel.key = getRandomHexString(48) (Channel.java line 36), HistoryKeeper.key = getRandomHexString(16) (HistoryKeeper.java line 36), and each session's user name = getRandomHexString(32) (NetfluxEndpoint.java line 174). The endpoint treats the channel key as the sole bearer capability, unlike the crypto modules which consistently use SecureRandom.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated SSRF via OIDC authorization endpoint `request_uri` parameter
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In AuthorizationEndpointRequestParserProcessor.parseRequest, the attacker-supplied OIDC `request_uri` query/form parameter (OIDCLoginProtocol.REQUEST_URI_PARAM) is passed verbatim to `session.getProvider(HttpClientProvider.class).get(requestUriParam)`. There is no validation that the URL is HTTPS, that its host is registered for the client (the OIDCClientRepresentation.request_uris value is never consumed anywhere in the server), or that it does not target loopback/link-local/internal addresses. The default client setting `request.object.required` is unset (treated as 'not required'), so any enabled client (including a public client whose client_id is public) can be used. The response stream is then read with no size limit (StreamUtil.readString) before being parsed as a JWS request object, and the parse failure is reported as a generic invalid_request, leaving a blind SSRF. The outbound client itself performs a plain HttpGet with a shared connection pool and default redirect handling (DefaultHttpClientFactory.get).

records.claim_title: HTTP/2 negative stream flow-control window causes indefinitely blocked response writes (remote DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Flow-control window reductions are applied without a lower bound and the blocking-write wait loop only detects exhaustion when the window is exactly zero. `Http2UpgradeHandler.setting()` applies `diff = (int)(value - oldValue)` from a client SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE to every existing Stream (Http2UpgradeHandler.java:1458-1473) and `AbstractStream.incrementWindowSize()` accepts negative results (AbstractStream.java:115-136); only an upper bound is validated (`ConnectionSettingsBase.validateInitialWindowSize`, ConnectionSettingsBase.java:198-204). `Stream.reserveWindowSize()` then loops `while (windowSize < 1)` but after `wait(writeTimeout)` only calls `doWriteTimeout()` when `windowSize == 0` (Stream.java:270-297, especially 284-287). For a negative window the timeout branch is unreachable, so the waiting writer loops on 20 s waits forever instead of timing out and closing the stream. The connection-level equivalent does handle exhaustion (`value[1] == 0` check in Http2UpgradeHandler.reserveWindowSize, Http2UpgradeHandler.java:801-828), so the missing negative-window handling is specific to the stream-level path.

records.claim_title: HTTP request smuggling via whitespace between header name and colon in HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader() terminates the header field-name at the first whitespace character (Character.isWhitespace) and then scans forward to the colon, so a line such as 'Transfer-Encoding : chunked' is parsed as name=Transfer-Encoding, value=chunked. The whitespace is discarded before the name reaches DefaultHttpHeaders.HttpNameValidator, which would otherwise reject a space inside a header name. The decoder therefore silently accepts and canonicalizes a header line that other HTTP components reject or parse differently, and the canonicalized name is used unchanged for body-framing decisions (Transfer-Encoding / Content-Length).

records.claim_title: HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame flood protection is defined but never installed (dead security control), enabling remote DoS
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame limiter is present but unreachable. Http2EmptyDataFrameListener implements the intended ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM cutoff, and Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder is designed to install that listener by overriding frameListener(...). However, no code in the repository ever constructs Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder: repo-wide searches for Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder, new Http2EmptyDataFrame, and maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames return only the two class definitions. AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder never wraps its decoder (build/buildFromConnection/buildFromCodec, lines 467-534), has no maxConsecutiveEmptyDataFrames field or accessor (only the sibling maxQueuedControlFrames at lines 110 and 330-351), and Http2CodecUtil only defines DEFAULT_MAX_QUEUED_CONTROL_FRAMES (line 135), with no default for consecutive empty DATA frames. Http2FrameCodecBuilder (lines 123-131) and Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder (lines 152-160) likewise expose only the control-frame knob. Consequently, empty DATA frames are delivered with no limit and no teardown.

records.claim_title: HTTP/1 field-line parser silently rewrites malformed header syntax (whitespace before/in field-name), enabling header interpretation mismatches and smuggling/splitting
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader() derives the field-name by stopping at the first whitespace character and then searching forward for ':' instead of requiring the colon to immediately follow the field-name (or rejecting the line). readHeaders() feeds the resulting name/value pair to the HttpHeaders without validating the original wire grammar, and the line parser additionally accepts bare-LF terminators and drops bare CR bytes. Framing-relevant headers (Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding) are therefore computed from a normalized view that can differ from strict HTTP parsers.

records.claim_title: RegexRequestMatcher can fail to match URLs containing decoded line terminators, causing URL security constraints to be skipped
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RegexRequestMatcher builds the match target from servletPath + pathInfo + queryString and evaluates it with pattern.matcher(url).matches() (web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/util/matcher/RegexRequestMatcher.java:85-113). Patterns are compiled with only CASE_INSENSITIVE when requested and without DOTALL, and no rejection/normalization of CR/LF is performed (lines 66-75). In Java regex, '.' does not match line terminators by default, so a pattern such as "/admin/.*" evaluated with Matcher.matches() against a value containing a decoded newline (e.g. "/admin/secret\n") does not match the entire region. When the matcher returns false, DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource.getAttributes returns null (web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/access/intercept/DefaultFilterInvocationSecurityMetadataSource.java:91-100), and AbstractSecurityInterceptor.beforeInvocation treats null/empty attributes as a public invocation, logging 'Public object - authentication not attempted' and returning without an access decision (core/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/access/intercept/AbstractSecurityInterceptor.java:199-216; rejectPublicInvocations defaults to false at line 121). The container can still resolve the same request to the protected path once the line terminator is normalized/stripped, producing a constraint bypass for applications that secure URLs solely with regex matchers and do not have a catch-all rule.

records.claim_title: Untrusted xop:Include/@href is fetched as a URL during MTOM attachment resolution (SSRF / local file read)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: CXF resolves the attacker-controlled href of an incoming <xop:Include> element by constructing a URL and a URLDataSource whenever the value contains "://", instead of restricting resolution to attachments that were actually received (cid:/message attachments). In core/src/main/java/org/apache/cxf/attachment/AttachmentUtil.java#getAttachmentDataSource (lines 525-544) the branches are: href starting with "cid:" -> loadDataSource, href without "://" -> loadDataSource (validated against the received attachment collection by LazyDataSource), and otherwise `new URLDataSource(new URL(contentId))` (lines 536-541). The URL branch ignores the attachments collection entirely and performs no scheme/host allow-listing, so hrefs such as http://169.254.169.254/…, http://internal-host/… or file:///etc/passwd are fetched when the returned DataSource/DataHandler is read (JAXBAttachmentUnmarshaller.getAttachmentAsByteArray immediately reads the stream; getAttachmentAsDataHandler defers until the application reads the handler). The legacy Aegis module contains the same flawed fallback in rt/databinding/aegis/src/main/java/org/apache/cxf/aegis/type/mtom/AttachmentUtil.java#getAttachment (lines 51-78): if the href matches no received attachment, it falls back to `new URLDataSource(new URL(id))` (lines 71-77), and AbstractXOPType.readInclude (lines 125-140) + ByteArrayType.readAttachment (lines 42-51) read that URL eagerly.

records.claim_title: Message headers supply the template and template resource URI in Velocity/FreeMarker/MVEL/Mustache producers (SSTI → RCE)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The templating producer endpoints treat message headers as trusted configuration instead of untrusted input. In onExchange they read the script/template text and the template resource URI from headers (VelocityConstants.VELOCITY_TEMPLATE / VELOCITY_RESOURCE_URI, FreemarkerConstants.FREEMARKER_TEMPLATE / FREEMARKER_RESOURCE_URI, MvelConstants.MVEL_TEMPLATE / MVEL_RESOURCE_URI, MustacheConstants.MUSTACHE_TEMPLATE / MUSTACHE_RESOURCE_URI), compile/load them, and evaluate them with a data model built from the Exchange. There is no validation, whitelist, or opt-in flag: a grep of the whole tree shows no 'allowTemplateFromHeader' (or equivalent) option, i.e. this is the pre-hardening behavior that later Camel releases changed to default-deny. A resource-URI header is even used to create a new endpoint via CamelContext.getEndpoint() and re-enter onExchange, so the template source (including file:/classpath: resources) is attacker-chosen as well.
