records.claim_title: HTTP/1 decoder accepts both Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Content-Length without normalization, enabling request smuggling
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: HttpObjectDecoder.readHeaders decides body framing by checking HttpUtil.isTransferEncodingChunked(message) first and, when true, moves to READ_CHUNK_SIZE without rejecting, removing, or otherwise normalizing a coexisting Content-Length header; the parsed Content-Length remains attached to the message (lines 573-598, 605-614). The non-chunked path derives length via HttpUtil.getContentLength, which reads only the first Content-Length value through headers().get(...) and parses it with Long.parseLong without validating duplicate/conflicting or malformed values (HttpUtil.java 174-189), and isTransferEncodingChunked only matches an exact 'chunked' value (HttpUtil.java 303-305). No compensating normalization exists in the outbound path either: HttpObjectEncoder frames by the TE header and its sanitizeHeadersBeforeEncode is a no-op (lines 90-101, 226-231), HttpRequestEncoder adds no sanitization (28-79), and HttpObjectAggregator removes only the TE header while retaining the attacker's Content-Length (204-242). Thus decoded and re-encoded messages carry contradictory framing metadata.

records.claim_title: camel-rabbitmq: attacker-triggered Java deserialization of AMQP message bodies (missing allowMessageBodySerialization gate)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RabbitMQMessageConverter.populateMessageBody()/deserializeBody() uses an unrestricted ObjectInputStream.readObject() on the AMQP message body based solely on the CamelSerialize header from raw AMQP BasicProperties (hasSerializeHeader/isSerializeHeaderEnabled), with no endpoint option or class allowlist. The producer side (RabbitMQMessagePublisher.publish) likewise unconditionally Java-serializes any Serializable body when no type converter is available and marks it with CamelSerialize. records.claim_title: YARN NodeManager ContainerLogsPage path traversal: unvalidated 'log.type' parameter allows arbitrary local file read
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In ContainerLogsPage.ContainersLogsBlock.printLogs() the request-supplied log type value (YarnWebParams.CONTAINER_LOG_TYPE = "log.type") is appended directly to the container log directory path and handed to LocalDirsHandlerService.getLogPathToRead(); LocalDirAllocator.getLocalPathToRead() joins it with each configured log directory via new Path(dir, pathStr) and only checks existence. Hadoop's Path constructor runs the URI through normalize(), which resolves '.'/'..' segments (and converts backslashes on Windows), so a value containing traversal sequences escapes the log root. The resulting File is opened with new FileInputStream(logFile) and its bytes are echoed to the HTTP response. There is no containment check and no validation of the parameter (no rejection of '/', '\', '..', or of values that resolve outside the log dirs).

records.claim_title: Untrusted Java deserialization in the Geode Management REST API (POST /geode-mgmt/v1/mbean/query) leading to RCE
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The production management webapp registers `SerializableObjectHttpMessageConverter` in geode-mgmt-servlet.xml. The converter advertises `MediaType.ALL` and `supports()` any `Serializable` parameter type, and its `readInternal` deserializes the raw HTTP request body with `IOUtils.deserializeObject(...)` -> `ObjectInputStream.readObject()` (via the unfiltered `ClassLoaderObjectInputStream`). `ShellCommandsController.queryNames(@RequestBody QueryParameterSource)` uses a `Serializable` domain class as the body type, so Spring selects this converter and deserializes attacker bytes before the handler runs; `type.cast(...)` happens only after deserialization, so gadget side effects execute even when the payload is not a `QueryParameterSource`. Geode's own serialization filter (`InternalDataSerializer.serializationFilter`/`ObjectInputStreamFilterWrapper`, applied via `setFilterOn` for Geode client/server streams) is not applied on this path.

records.claim_title: XStreamer applies attacker-supplied XStream instance (and its type permissions) to the untrusted payload, bypassing the security framework
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XStreamer.fromXML() first unmarshals an XStream instance out of the same attacker-controlled stream, then uses that deserialized instance - including its SecurityMapper.permissions list - to unmarshal the rest of the stream. The outer permission set (XStreamer.PERMISSIONS, or the caller-supplied TypePermission... overload) only restricts the class graph of the embedded XStream object; it deliberately allows the XStream, Mapper and TypePermission hierarchies. Because type permissions are ordinary instance state of the embedded SecurityMapper, an attacker can embed an XStream configured with AnyTypePermission.ANY (or any permissive permission) and thereby replace the effective whitelist for the payload.

records.claim_title: LDAP filter injection via unescaped X.509 selector values in LDAP CertStore/LDAPStoreHelper
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Both LDAP directory implementations build LDAP filters by direct string concatenation of caller-supplied DN-derived values. In X509LDAPCertStoreSpi.search a filter is built as attributeName + "=" + attributeValue, where attributeValue is "*" + parseDN(subject, ...) + "*" (the selector's subject/issuer), and is then embedded in "(&(" + filter + ")(" + attr + "=*))" and passed to DirContext.search. In LDAPStoreHelper.search the same pattern is used: filter += "(" + attributeNames[i] + "=" + attributeValue + ")". No escaping of LDAP filter metacharacters ('*', '(', ')', '\\', NUL) or rejection of them exists anywhere in the tree (searches for escapeFilter/RFC2254 returned nothing), so filter syntax supplied through the selector survives into the executed query.

records.claim_title: SSL hostname verification silently skipped for ssl=true and for verify-full with a custom SSLSocketFactory
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MakeSSL.convert decides hostname verification from the raw `sslmode` property and the concrete factory type instead of the driver's effective SSL mode (`SslMode.of`, which maps `ssl=true` to VERIFY_FULL). (1) Lines 35-45: when `sslmode` is null (i.e. `ssl=true`, the documented way to request verified SSL) the driver uses `SSLSocketFactory.getDefault()` (JSSE default with no endpoint identification and the JVM CA store instead of `root.crt`). (2) Lines 71-98: hostname verification is attempted only if `sslhostnameverifier` is explicitly set, or if `"verify-full".equals(sslmode) && factory instanceof LibPQFactory`; therefore with `sslmode=verify-full&sslfactory=<custom>` the identity check is skipped entirely, and with `ssl=true` it never runs at all. Hostname checking exists (jdbc4.LibPQFactory.verify / unused PGjdbcHostnameVerifier) but is not invoked in these configurations, and the SSLSocket never gets an endpoint-identification algorithm set.

records.claim_title: XXE/SSRF via pooled SAX parser without external-entity restrictions, reachable through default XLSX parsing
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The SAXParserFactory used for all pooled SAX parsers (tika-core XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParserFactory(), lines 163-181) enables only XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING. FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING is a parser-DoS/entity-expansion limit, not an external-access block - the codebase itself relies on OfflineContentHandler to stop 'network or other external resources from being accessed by an XML parser' (OfflineContentHandler javadoc). records.claim_title: OS command injection via unquoted archive path in FileUtil.unTar() reachable from YARN resource localization
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: FileUtil.unTarUsingTar() builds a shell command string and executes it via `bash -c`. In the non-gzipped branch it appends `FileUtil.makeShellPath(inFile)` directly after `tar -xf ` with no quoting or escaping (FileUtil.java lines 664-670). On Unix, makeShellPath(String) is a no-op that only returns the input filename (FileUtil.java lines 514-516), so any shell metacharacter in the file name (;, $(), backticks, quotes, spaces, etc.) is interpreted by bash. FSDownload derives the localized file name from the application-controlled LocalResource URL and passes it to FileUtil.unTar(), turning the utility into an injection sink for a job owner.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Jenkins CLI remoting endpoints create a master-side remoting channel and deserialize attacker-supplied Java objects before authentication
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `CLIAction` is an `UnprotectedRootAction` bound to `/cli`; its `getTarget()` routes any POST to `/cli` (without `remoting=false`) into `RemotingCliEndpointResponse` whenever `jenkins.CLI` is enabled, explicitly without any permission check (code comment: "do not require any permission to establish a CLI connection"). That response builds a full-duplex remoting `Channel` over the HTTP streams. Independently, the TCP agent protocol handlers `CliProtocol.Handler.run()/runCli()` and `CliProtocol2.Handler2.run()` accept a connection, exchange a greeting (and, for CLI2, a DH key), and immediately build a remoting `Channel` with `.withBaseLoader(Jenkins.getActiveInstance().pluginManager.uberClassLoader)`; nothing authenticates the peer before `channel.join()` begins reading and deserializing remoting requests/arguments. `CliManagerImpl.main()` (the `CliEntryPoint` implementation installed on the channel) is only reached after that deserialization has already happened, so per-command permission checks in `CLICommand.main()` are too late to prevent gadget-chain deserialization.

records.claim_title: Archive extraction in hudson.FilePath does not prevent zip/tar entry path traversal (Zip/Tar Slip) — arbitrary file write
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `FilePath.unzip(File,File)` (core/src/main/java/hudson/FilePath.java:590-624) and `FilePath.readFromTar(...)` (core/src/main/java/hudson/FilePath.java:2291-2323) build the destination with `new File(dir, e.getName())` / `new File(baseDir, te.getName())` and then call `mkdirs(...)`/`writing(f)`/`IOUtils.copy(...)` without ever verifying that the resolved path stays inside `dir`/`baseDir`. No canonical-path check, no rejection of `..` path segments, and no restriction on tar symlink targets (`new FilePath(f).symlinkTo(te.getLinkName(), ...)`) exists in this class (`getCanonicalPath`/`getCanonicalFile` is never used in FilePath). The only helper that runs before writes, `writing(File f)` (FilePath.java:2906-2915), merely invokes `FilePathFilter` (default allow) and does not normalize or bound the path. Entry names come from the archive (`org.apache.tools.zip.ZipEntry#getName`, `TarArchiveEntry#getName`), which preserve `../`/`..\` sequences, so `new File(dir, "../../x")` escapes.

records.claim_title: SnakeYamlEngine deserializes untrusted request bodies with SnakeYAML's unsafe constructor (arbitrary type instantiation, potential RCE)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SnakeYamlEngine.fromString(String content, Class<T> classOfT) ignores the requested target type and unconditionally calls `new Yaml().load(content)`. The no-arg Yaml constructor uses SnakeYAML's non-safe Constructor, which builds objects of any Java class named by YAML tags and populates their bean properties. There is no SafeConstructor, LoaderOptions type restriction, or whitelist anywhere in the module or repository (searched "SafeConstructor", "new Yaml", "snakeyaml"), and the module pins SnakeYAML 1.17. In the same parent module the analogous XStream engine was hardened with xstream.allowTypes(...) from the Pippo deserialization whitelist (CHANGELOG #454), showing the intended security posture; SnakeYAML was left unrestricted. It is auto-registered for `application/x-yaml` by the @MetaInfServices SnakeYamlInitializer on the classpath.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 and 0-10 length fields drive unbounded heap allocation (DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The 0-8-family and 0-10 deserializers trust 32-bit wire length fields when sizing Java arrays. EncodingUtils.readBytes() reads an unsigned 32-bit length and immediately executes new byte[(int)length] before any check that the remaining buffer contains that many bytes (same pattern in readLongString/readLongstr). The 0-10 AbstractDecoder does the same in get(int) and readVbin32(). The subsequent buffer.get(...) can only fail after the oversized allocation has already been attempted. Values > Integer.MAX_VALUE wrap negative and merely raise NegativeArraySizeException, but every value <= 0x7FFFFFFF produces a real allocation attempt of up to ~2 GiB from a frame that itself is capped at a few hundred/thousand bytes.

records.claim_title: Server-side snapshot name is not validated, allowing path traversal in filesystem operations (arbitrary directory deletion/write)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Snapshot names supplied by RPC clients are validated only in the client library (ClientSnapshotDescriptionUtils.assertSnapshotRequestIsValid -> TableName.isLegalTableQualifierName(..., true)), not on the server. MasterRpcServices.deleteSnapshot passes request.getSnapshot() straight to SnapshotManager.deleteSnapshot, and MasterRpcServices.snapshot only calls SnapshotDescriptionUtils.validate(), which checks table presence/creation-time/ACL but never the snapshot name. SnapshotDescriptionUtils.getCompletedSnapshotDir/getWorkingSnapshotDir then build paths as new Path(snapshotsDir, snapshotName) (Hadoop Path(parent, child) performs URI resolution that resolves '..' and accepts absolute children), so '..'/absolute-path snapshot names escape the .snapshot directory. SnapshotManager then uses those resolved paths in destructive filesystem operations: recursive delete of the working dir before creating a snapshot, recursive delete of the completed snapshot dir, mkdirs and rename.

records.claim_title: CGI servlet runs the resolved program even after the docroot/canonical-path validation decides to reject it (missing return after 404)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In CGI.service(), when useFullPath is false, the requested path is resolved to a program under _docRoot and then validated with `if (path.length()==0 || !execCmd.exists() || execCmd.isDirectory() || !execCmd.getCanonicalPath().equals(execCmd.getAbsolutePath()))`. The failure branch only calls `res.sendError(404)` and falls through (no `return`), so `pathInfo = info` and `exec(execCmd, pathInfo, req, res)` execute unconditionally; exec() contains no re-validation and calls `Runtime.getRuntime().exec(execCmd, env.getEnvArray(), _docRoot)` (line 352). The denial decision is therefore ignored and a command that the check explicitly classified as invalid (empty path, directory, or non-canonical/aliased path) is executed anyway.

records.claim_title: HTTP/2 control-frame flood mitigation is dead code: Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder is never installed, allowing unbounded queued PING/SETTINGS/RST responses (remote DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder (codec-http2) is defined but referenced nowhere in the repository: no `new Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder(...)` exists and the identifier occurs only inside its own file. The HTTP/2 connection builders build the encoder chain as `new DefaultHttp2ConnectionEncoder(connection, writer)` (plus optional StreamBufferingEncoder) without ever decorating it with the limiter, and Http2ConnectionHandler stores/uses that encoder directly. Consequently the counter/limit logic (flush, then connectionError(ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM) and ctx.close() once maxOutstandingControlFrames outstanding control frames are reached) can never execute, while the decoder still auto-acknowledges every PING and SETTINGS frame by default.

records.claim_title: SSRF via untrusted `Long-Running-Action` header in the LRA saga EIP
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The saga EIP treats the message header `Exchange.SAGA_LONG_RUNNING_ACTION` ("Long-Running-Action") as the identifier of an existing saga without any validation of its content or origin. `SagaProcessor.getCurrentSagaCoordinator()` passes the header value directly to `CamelSagaService.getSaga(String)`. For the LRA implementation, `LRASagaService.getSaga()` executes `new URL(id)` and wraps it in `LRASagaCoordinator`, whose `beginStep()/compensate()/complete()` delegate to `LRAClient`, which builds a JAX-RS `WebTarget` from that URL (`client.target(lra.toString())`) and sends PUT requests. There is no check that the URL/authority matches the configured `coordinatorUrl`, and the header is not filtered by any HTTP/JMS header filter strategy (those only match the `Camel`/`org.apache.camel` pattern).

records.claim_title: HTTP/1.1 processor is not released on a direct h2c upgrade, leaking processors and enabling memory-exhaustion DoS
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In AbstractProtocol.ConnectionHandler.process() the direct HTTP/2 (h2c) branch handles SocketState.UPGRADING with a null UpgradeToken by obtaining a new HTTP/2 processor and calling wrapper.setCurrentProcessor(processor), but it never calls release(processor) for the HTTP/1.1 processor that processed the connection so far. The parallel non-direct upgrade branch at lines 870-874 does call release(processor). Because the HTTP/1.1 processor was registered in JMX at creation (register(), lines 1072-1097), the MBean server keeps a RequestProcessor MBean -> RequestInfo -> Request -> hook -> processor reference chain alive; without release()/recycle() that whole graph (processor, request/response, buffers, socket wrapper) is never reclaimed and its MBean is never unregistered (RecycledProcessors.push() unregisters only when a released processor cannot be cached, lines 1155-1168).

records.claim_title: CiphertextHeaderV2 decodes untrusted key name without an effective length bound (undefined MAX_KEYNAME_LEN; stream EOF never terminates) leading to unbounded memory growth / hang
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In CiphertextHeaderV2.decodeInternal (src/main/java/org/cryptacular/CiphertextHeaderV2.java), the symbolic key name is read byte-by-byte from attacker-supplied header data in `while ((b = readByteFn.apply(source)) != 0)` and accumulated in a ByteArrayOutputStream. The only intended cap, `if (out.size() > MAX_KEYNAME_LEN)` (line 204), cannot take effect because MAX_KEYNAME_LEN is not declared anywhere in the repository (repository-wide search finds only this single reference), and the encoding/decoding helpers it relies on (ByteUtil.toUnsignedByte(int), ByteUtil.toInt(Byte), ByteUtil.toString(byte[],int,int)) are likewise absent. In the InputStream overload, readByte() returns `(byte) input.read()`; at EOF input.read() returns -1, which becomes 0xFF (nonzero), so the sentinel condition is never met and the loop appends forever, growing memory until OOM (and hanging the caller). Parsing occurs before HMAC verification, so no key material is needed to trigger it.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Java deserialization of HTTP request bodies in the default Camel HTTP bindings (camel-http / camel-http4 / camel-jetty / camel-servlet)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultHttpBinding.readRequest() inspects only the client-supplied Content-Type header and, when it equals `application/x-java-serialized-object`, converts the raw request body to an InputStream and calls HttpHelper.deserializeJavaObjectFromStream(), which does `new ObjectInputStream(is).readObject()` with no class allow-list, no type filter, no size limit, and no configuration switch to disable it. The same code is duplicated in camel-http4. Because HttpEndpoint.getBinding() lazily returns `new DefaultHttpBinding(this)` when no binding is configured, this is the default behavior of the camel-http/camel-http4 HttpMessage-based consumers (camel-jetty's CamelContinuationServlet and camel-servlet's CamelHttpTransportServlet extend camel-http's CamelServlet, which constructs an HttpMessage per request; JettyRestHttpBinding and ServletRestHttpBinding used by the REST DSL also extend DefaultHttpBinding). The attacker therefore controls the bytes that are deserialized while the trusted application supplies the vulnerable reader.

records.claim_title: Path traversal in Expander.expand writes outside target directory via sibling-directory prefix bypass
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Expander.expand(ArchiveEntrySupplier, EntryWriter, File) computes `String targetDirPath = targetDirectory.getCanonicalPath()` (Expander.java:241) and validates each entry with `if (!f.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(targetDirPath))` (Expander.java:244-248). A plain String.startsWith on a canonical path does not enforce directory containment: if a sibling directory exists whose canonical path extends the target's canonical path (e.g. target `/data/out`, sibling `/data/out-old`), an entry name such as `../out-old/file` canonicalizes to `/data/out-old/file`, which still startsWith `/data/out`. The check passes and the file is created via `Files.newOutputStream(f.toPath())` (Expander.java:258-259), after `parent.mkdirs()` (Expander.java:254-257). There is no trailing File.separator, no java.nio.file.Path component-wise comparison, and no `..`/name sanitization anywhere in the class.

records.claim_title: Unbounded/cyclic 7z folder stream-graph walk in Folder.getOrderedCoders() enables infinite loop, unbounded memory growth and out-of-range index access
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The 7z folder structure parsed from the archive header is trusted. SevenZFile.readFolder() (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/SevenZFile.java:560-637) reads numCoders, per-coder in/out stream counts, the bind pairs (inIndex/outIndex, SevenZFile.java:604-611) and packedStreams (SevenZFile.java:616-634) directly from the untrusted header and validates only two conditions: totalOutputStreams != 0 (lines 601-603) and totalInStreams >= numBindPairs (lines 613-615). Bind-pair indices are neither range-checked, nor required to be unique, nor required to form an acyclic graph. Folder.getOrderedCoders() (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/sevenz/Folder.java:54-63) then walks that unvalidated graph with an unbounded while (current != -1) loop, following findBindPairForOutStream() (Folder.java:74-81) and appending to a LinkedList every iteration, with no visited set, iteration cap or index bounds check. A crafted bind-pair graph containing a cycle reachable from the packed-stream index (possible because duplicate inIndex values are accepted, for example pairs (in=0,out=3), (in=1,out=0), (in=0,out=1) with packedStreams[0]=3) makes current oscillate forever while l.addLast(coders[current]) grows the list without bound. Independently, int current = (int) packedStreams[0] and (int) bindPairs[pair].inIndex narrow 64-bit header values to int with no range check, so coders[current] can be indexed out of range or negatively.

records.claim_title: Infinite loop in ZIP file-name encoding (NioZipEncoding.encode / encodeFully) for non-UTF-8 charsets
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: NioZipEncoding.encode (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/NioZipEncoding.java:85-116) loops while the character buffer has remaining input, but only reacts to CoderResult.isUnmappable()/isMalformed() and isOverflow(). There is no branch for a non-consuming UNDERFLOW result (or any other non-error, non-overflow result), so if CharsetEncoder.encode(cb, out, false) returns without consuming input the loop spins forever. In the unmappable/malformed branch, each offending character is re-encoded through encodeFully (lines 136-146), which also only handles isOverflow(): it grows the buffer and retries, but never consumes/aborts on unmappable or malformed results. encodeSurrogate (lines 148-159) builds the escape from the ASCII characters '%', 'U', '0'-'9', 'A'-'F'; if the target charset's encoder reports such characters as unmappable (or otherwise returns a non-consuming result), encodeFully never advances and never grows, producing an unbounded loop. ZipEncodingHelper.getZipEncoding (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/compress/archivers/zip/ZipEncodingHelper.java:54-64) enables escape-based encoding (useReplacement=false, i.e., REPORT error actions) for every charset except UTF-8, so non-UTF-8/default-charset environments take the vulnerable branch.

records.claim_title: DiskFileItem deserialization uses attacker-controlled repository/content without validation (missing repository check)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `DiskFileItem` is Serializable (`FileItem extends Serializable`) and serializes its `repository` File field, `sizeThreshold`, `cachedContent` and `dfosFile`. `readObject` calls `in.defaultReadObject()` and then unconditionally opens an output stream via `getOutputStream()` -> `getTempFile()`, which builds `new File(repository, "upload_<UID>_<counter>.tmp")` from the deserialized `repository` and writes the deserialized `cachedContent` (or copies from the deserialized `dfosFile` path) into it. There is no validation that the deserialized repository is a legitimate/valid directory: `isDirectory`/`InvalidObjectException` do not appear anywhere in the snapshot, and `DiskFileItem` imports no validation API. This directly contradicts the repository's own changelog entry for 1.3.1, which states this hardening was made. The permanent `UID`/counter file naming and the `fileName` sanitization do not constrain the attacker-chosen repository directory or the written bytes.

records.claim_title: Missing MultipartStream buffer-size validation allows remote DoS via oversized multipart boundary (CVE-2014-0050 class)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The public MultipartStream constructor (src/main/java/org/apache/commons/fileupload/MultipartStream.java:323-344) stores the caller-supplied bufSize and allocates the buffer without ever checking that it can hold the boundary: boundaryLength = boundary.length + 4 and keepRegion = boundaryLength, buffer length = bufSize, with no requirement bufSize >= boundaryLength + 1. When boundaryLength >= bufSize, findSeparator() (lines 697-718) always computes maxpos = tail - boundaryLength < 0 and returns -1; ItemInputStream.findSeparator() (817-826) then sets pad = tail - head (because tail-head <= keepRegion), so available() (845-851) returns 0, and makeAvailable() (983-1017) repeatedly calls input.read(buffer, tail, bufSize - tail) which returns 0 once tail == bufSize, never reaching -1 or finding a separator. The for(;;) loop therefore never terminates and never progresses. The snapshot's own changes.xml (lines 54-60) documents the intended fix: 'Fix CVE-2014-0050 ... enforce the requirements for buffer size by throwing an IllegalArgumentException if the requested buffer size is too small.' That code does not exist (no IllegalArgumentException, and no 'too small' message, anywhere in the tree).

records.claim_title: BMP BI_BITFIELDS with a zero color mask hangs forever in PixelParserBitFields.getMaskShift (CWE-835 DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `getMaskShift(int mask)` computes the shift for a BMP color mask with `while ((0x1 & mask) == 0) { mask = 0x7fffffff & (mask >> 1); trailingZeroes++; }`. For `mask == 0` the body leaves `mask` at 0, so the exit condition remains false forever and the loop is effectively infinite (the incremented counter is not part of the condition, so even its integer wrap does not terminate it). The only guard in the constructor is for the alpha mask (`alphaShift = (alphaMask != 0 ? getMaskShift(alphaMask) : 0)`); `redMask`, `greenMask` and `blueMask` are passed to `getMaskShift` with no non-zero check and are read directly from the attacker-controlled BMP header when `compression == BI_BITFIELDS` (or `bitmapHeaderSize >= 52`). No validation of the masks exists in `readBmpHeaderInfo` or `readImageContents`.

records.claim_title: Non-terminating loop in BMP BI_BITFIELDS mask handling on a zero colour mask (uninterruptible 100% CPU hang)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: PixelParserBitFields.getMaskShift(int mask) computes the shift for a bitfield mask with `while ((0x1 & mask) == 0) { mask = 0x7fffffff & (mask >> 1); trailingZeroes++; }`. For mask == 0 the loop body leaves mask at 0 and the exit condition can never become true, so the method never returns. The constructor calls getMaskShift unconditionally for the file-derived red, green and blue masks (lines 51-53) but guards only the alpha mask (`alphaMask != 0 ? getMaskShift(alphaMask) : 0`, line 54), and nothing validates that the masks read from the BMP header are non-zero. records.claim_title: FilenameUtils.normalize() leaves '..' in UNC-like paths, bypassing path-traversal sanitization
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: getPrefixLength() treats any separator-delimited text as a valid UNC hostname, rejecting only an empty host (FilenameUtils.java:671-679). It therefore accepts "." and ".." as the "server" part (prefix = length including the following separator, e.g. 5 for "//../foo"). doNormalize() then starts its double-dot scan at i = prefix + 2 (:408), so the "../" that lies inside the prefix region (indices 2-4) is never examined or removed; no post-hoc validation of the result exists, and the method returns the unmodified string via new String(array, 0, size - 1) (:443). The contract documented in the same file (:179, :185) says such inputs should return null.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: AttachmentUtil.getAttachmentDataSource() (core/src/main/java/org/apache/cxf/attachment/AttachmentUtil.java:520-539) only special-cases references starting with "cid:" or containing no "://"; every other value is treated as an absolute URL and wrapped in javax.activation.URLDataSource(new URL(contentId)) (line 533) with no allow-list of schemes/hosts. records.claim_title: Malformed URI authority is decoded and mis-split when deriving the request target host, so a request can be executed against an unintended host
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In URIUtils.extractHost (httpclient/src/main/java/org/apache/http/client/utils/URIUtils.java, lines 333-387), when java.net.URI cannot parse the authority as server-based (uri.getHost() == null), the fallback takes the DECODED authority (host = uri.getAuthority(), line 343) and removes everything up to the FIRST decoded '@' (line 346), then silently ignores a non-numeric port suffix (lines 354-374). RFC 3986 requires the userinfo delimiter to be a literal '@' and a valid port to be digits, so a percent-encoded '@' (e.g. %40) inside the authority is wrongly treated as the userinfo separator and an invalid port is dropped. The resulting HttpHost is returned as the request target and is used for route planning and the actual DNS/TCP connection. records.claim_title: Unbounded /Prev xref-chain loop in COSParser.parseXref (crafted-PDF infinite loop / DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `COSParser.parseXref()` follows the trailer `/Prev` chain with `while (prev > 0)` and reassigns `prev` directly from the parsed, file-controlled trailer value, without recording visited offsets. When `/Prev` points to the current (or any already-parsed) xref offset, `checkXRefOffset(prev)` finds a valid `xref` keyword at `prev` and returns that same offset (COSParser.java:1173-1176), so the loop re-parses the identical bytes forever. The same applies to the xref-stream branch, because `parseXrefObjStream()` returns `dict.getLong(COSName.PREV)` (COSParser.java:330). The sibling `XrefTrailerResolver.setStartxref()` contains a 'sanity check to prevent infinite loops' (XrefTrailerResolver.java:258-262), but it runs only after `parseXref()` has already completed, so it cannot stop this loop.

records.claim_title: Unbounded beginbfrange expansion in fontbox CMapParser (crafted PDF CMap) causes CPU exhaustion / OutOfMemoryError
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: CMapParser.parseBeginbfrange() derives the number of generated mappings from attacker-supplied hex codes with no sanity limit. The loop at fontbox/src/main/java/org/apache/fontbox/cmap/CMapParser.java:382-407 is controlled solely by `compare(startCode, endCode)`, i.e. the lexicographic distance between the two codes in the `beginbfrange` entry, and increments startCode per iteration (increment() at lines 678-694). For 3- or 4-byte codes the distance can be up to 2^24 / 2^32. Each iteration calls CMap.addCharMapping() (fontbox/src/main/java/org/apache/fontbox/cmap/CMap.java:188-198), which allocates a String and inserts an entry into the `charToUnicode` HashMap (CMap.java:49), so both CPU use and retained heap grow with attacker-controlled magnitude. There is no cap on total mappings in CMapParser or CMap (`parse()` at CMapParser.java:88-136 has no size/count limit), and only the null/empty-token cases are guarded (lines 376-381, older PDFBOX-3450/3807 fixes).

records.claim_title: StAX signature verification uses attacker-supplied ds:KeyValue public key instead of the configured verification key
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `SecurityTokenFactoryImpl.setTokenKey`, the configured `securityProperties.getSignatureVerificationKey()` is installed on the token as its public key only when the token type is NOT `KeyValueToken` (`if (key instanceof PublicKey && !SecurityTokenConstants.KeyValueToken.equals(token.getTokenType()))`). For RSA/DSA/EC `ds:KeyValue` tokens the configured key is instead put into the secret-key table (`setSecretKey("", key)`), while `RsaKeyValueSecurityToken`/`DsaKeyValueSecurityToken`/`ECKeyValueSecurityToken.getPublicKey()` build the public key from the untrusted message whenever the token's `publicKey` field is null. The asymmetric verification path never consults the secret-key table: `AbstractInboundSecurityToken.getPubKey(...)` returns `getPublicKey()`, and `AbstractSignatureInputHandler.SignatureVerifier.createSignatureAlgorithm(...)` calls `inboundSecurityToken.getPublicKey(...)` for every `isAsymmetric()` token and initializes the JCE Signature with it. Consequently a message that merely includes a `ds:KeyValue` in the Signature's KeyInfo causes the library to verify the signature with the key embedded in that untrusted message rather than with the application's pinned key. The same factory uses the configured key when there is no KeyInfo (DefaultToken -> setPublicKey) and for X509 tokens, so the behavior is inconsistent and KeyInfo-controlled.

records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled rememberMe cookie is decrypted and Java-deserialized without integrity or class protection (and the repo ships a public cipher key in a sample)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Identity data for the rememberMe feature is read from an HTTP cookie fully controlled by the requester. `CookieRememberMeManager.getRememberedSerializedIdentity` only Base64-decodes the value; `AbstractRememberMeManager.convertBytesToPrincipals` then decrypts it with the configured symmetric key and passes the resulting plaintext directly to the configured `Serializer` — by default `DefaultSerializer`, which wraps it in `ClassResolvingObjectInputStream` and calls `readObject()` with no class allow-list and no integrity verification (no MAC/AEAD). Security therefore rests entirely on the secrecy of the symmetric key: the library generates a random key only when the application does not configure one, and it documents/ships configuration that uses a fixed, well-known key (`samples/guice/.../shiro.ini` line 29 sets `kPH+bIxk5D2deZiIxcaaaA==`, which `SampleShiroServletModule` (lines 74-79) reads and installs with `rememberMeManager.setCipherKey(Base64.decode(cipherKey))`). With a known/weak key (or a custom serializer such as `XmlSerializer`, whose `XMLDecoder.readObject()` is also an unsafe deserialization sink), an unauthenticated attacker can forge a remembered principal or submit a gadget chain that executes on deserialization. Note the file/line of the classic CVE-2016-4437 remedy (`setCipherKey(cipherService.generateNewKey().getEncoded())`, AbstractRememberMeManager lines 95-100) is present, which limits the plain default-config exposure.

records.claim_title: Unsafe Kryo deserialization of Sling Distribution package content (CWE-502)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: KryoContentSerializer.importFromStream() constructs a default Kryo instance (registrationRequired remains false), installs Kryo.DefaultInstantiatorStrategy with Objenesis StdInstantiatorStrategy, and calls kryo.readObject(input, LinkedList.class) directly on the package stream. Kryo's default class resolver reads class names from the stream, loads them with Class.forName and instantiates them (constructor bypass via StdInstantiatorStrategy) with no allow-list, so arbitrary classes on the classpath can be instantiated and their read/deserialization hooks invoked. records.claim_title: getValidHref() accepts undeclared HTML5 named entities, allowing javascript: scheme smuggling into href/src attributes
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: URL sanitization decodes only percent-encoding (URLDecoder) and XML entities (StringEscapeUtils.unescapeXml: the five predefined XML entities plus numeric references). Validation is then a whole-string whitelist (AntiSamy onsiteURL) whose character class deliberately permits '&', ';', '(', ')' for query strings. Named HTML5 character references such as `:` are not XML entities, so they are neither decoded during validation nor percent-encoded in the output. The result is that the returned string can still contain an HTML-character-reference-obfuscated scheme separator that the browser decodes when the value is placed in an attribute, defeating the javascript:-scheme check.

records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled multipart error text (filename) is evaluated as an OGNL expression via LocalizedTextUtil default-message translation
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Multipart error handling passes attacker-influenced exception text as the `defaultMessage` argument of `LocalizedTextUtil.findText(...)`, and `LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage()` unconditionally runs that default message through `TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack)`, which evaluates every `${...}`/`%{...}` fragment as an OGNL expression on the request value stack. In `JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest`, `addFileSkippedError()` embeds the client-supplied multipart filename in a `FileSizeLimitExceededException` message (`"Skipped file " + fileName + "; request size limit exceeded."`), and `buildErrorMessage()` passes that message as the default message; the lookup key is also never resolved (`struts.message.upload.error.` — singular — while the bundle defines `struts.messages.upload.error.*` only, and no `FileSizeLimitExceededException` entry exists), so untrusted text is always the string that gets OGNL-evaluated. `JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage()` and `MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage()` contain the same `e.getMessage()`-as-default-message pattern (same root cause, default-parser paths).

records.claim_title: Hard-coded 'class' access exclusion (ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN) is disabled in ParametersInterceptor and CookieInterceptor, re-enabling OGNL class-loader property injection
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The framework ships a hard-coded denylist for parameter/cookie names that traverse the OGNL 'class' property, but its enforcement is commented out at both call sites: (1) xwork-core ParametersInterceptor.setExcludeParams() replaces excludeParams with only the configured patterns and the line that adds the CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN is commented out (lines 510-511); (2) core CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName() returns only the permissive legacy `acceptedPattern.matcher(name).matches()` while the `ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN` check is commented out (lines 247-250). The constants class xwork-core ExcludedPatterns (CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN/EXCLUDED_PATTERNS, lines 7-20) now has zero reference from production code, and the default stacks only exclude ^action:.* and ^method:.* (core/src/main/resources/struts-default.xml lines 199-201, 255-257, 265-267, 302-304). Consequently attacker-controlled dotted names such as class.classLoader... pass acceptableName()/isAcceptableParameter() and are evaluated by OGNL with a member access whose exclude set no longer contains the class pattern.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In CookieInterceptor.isAcceptableName (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/interceptor/CookieInterceptor.java:247-250) the only check performed is `acceptedPattern.matcher(name).matches()`, whose default pattern is `[a-zA-Z0-9\.\]\[_'\s]+` (line 170/176). That pattern allows pure letter/dot/bracket/quote names, so names such as `class.classLoader.<property>` or `class['classLoader'].<property>` pass. The line that would reject such names is commented out (`// Patch: return !Pattern.compile(ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN).matcher(name).matches();`), and the class no longer imports/uses `ExcludedPatterns` at all, even though ExcludedPatterns.java's own Javadoc (xwork-core/.../ExcludedPatterns.java:4-5) says its patterns are used 'partially in CookInterceptor'. The accepted cookie name is later used directly as an OGNL expression: populateCookieValueIntoStack (lines 261-287) calls `stack.setValue(cookieName, cookieValue)` (lines 274/285).

records.claim_title: Predictable anti-CSRF tokens and attacker-selected token name in TokenInterceptor / TokenSessionStoreInterceptor
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/util/TokenHelper.java uses a shared instance of java.util.Random for security tokens (line 54: `private static final Random RANDOM = new Random();`; lines 226-228: `new BigInteger(165, RANDOM).toString(36).toUpperCase()`). java.util.Random is a 48-bit LCG; its outputs are recoverable from observed values and all sessions share one static instance, so tokens issued by TokenHelper.setToken() are predictable. In addition, TokenHelper.getTokenName() (lines 154-179) and getToken() (128-147) take the token name and token value directly from request parameters without any validation, and validToken() (187-224) uses `struts.tokens.` + attacker-chosen tokenName as the session key. TokenInterceptor.handleToken (lines 145-155) and TokenSessionStoreInterceptor.handleToken (lines 107-118) treat a true return from TokenHelper.validToken() as proof that the request came from the legitimate user's form.

records.claim_title: Attacker-controlled Content-Type header reaches OGNL evaluation via multipart error message (RCE)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Multipart parse errors keep the raw exception message (containing the attacker-supplied Content-Type header) as the localized error default message, and the localization fallback evaluates that default message as an OGNL expression. records.claim_title: Unauthenticated OGNL evaluation of attacker-controlled Content-Type via multipart error message
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The multipart error path passes attacker-influenced exception text as a localizable default message into an OGNL-evaluating lookup. JakartaMultiPartRequest.parse() catches parsing exceptions and buildErrorMessage() calls LocalizedTextUtil.findText(this.getClass(), key, locale, e.getMessage(), args) (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/multipart/JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:101-124). For commons-fileupload's InvalidContentTypeException the message text contains the raw request Content-Type header; the 'struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException' key is not defined in struts-messages*.properties (only SizeLimitExceededException and IOException are), so LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() falls back to that message and calls TextParseUtil.translateVariables(message, valueStack) (xwork-core/src/main/java/com/opensymphony/xwork2/util/LocalizedTextUtil.java:668-691, eval at 683), which parses and evaluates %{...} expressions on the action ValueStack via OgnlTextParser/stack.findValue. Because request wrapping happens before action mapping, any request whose Content-Type contains 'multipart/form-data' is parsed (core/src/main/java/org/apache/struts2/dispatcher/Dispatcher.java:831-847, check at 837-838; default parser 'jakarta' per core/src/main/resources/org/apache/struts2/default.properties:69 and struts-default.xml:92), so a Content-Type such as '%{<OGNL>}.multipart/form-data' is wrapped, rejected as a non-multipart content type with the raw header echoed in the exception message, and then evaluated as OGNL. The same pattern exists in sibling code: JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage/buildMessage (lines 538-557) and MultiPartRequestWrapper.buildErrorMessage (lines 106-112).

records.claim_title: OGNL expression evaluation of attacker-controlled Content-Type via multipart error message (S2-045 pattern)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() passes the parser exception message as the `defaultMessage` argument to LocalizedTextUtil.findText (core/.../JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:118-124). When the error key is not present in any bundle, LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage() runs TextParseUtil.translateVariables(defaultMessage, valueStack) on that text (xwork-core/.../LocalizedTextUtil.java:660-683), which delegates to OgnlTextParser and evaluates every ${...}/%{...} fragment with stack.findValue (TextParseUtil.java:157-172; OgnlTextParser.java:10-82). The exception message in question comes from commons-fileupload's invalid-content-type failure and embeds the raw Content-Type request header (the RequestContext exposes req.getContentType() verbatim at JakartaMultiPartRequest.java:358-366), so attacker-controlled header text is OGNL-evaluated. Dispatcher.wrapRequest() only requires the header to *contain* the literal `multipart/form-data` to route the request into the multipart wrapper (Dispatcher.java:828-841); a header that contains that substring but is not a valid multipart media type makes commons-fileupload raise InvalidContentTypeException, whose message carries the whole header.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated OGNL expression injection via multipart Content-Type error message (S2-045-style multipart parser flaw)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage() passes the raw exception message (e.getMessage()) as the defaultMessage argument of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(). When a request Content-Type contains the literal substring "multipart/form-data" (Dispatcher.wrapRequest gate) but does not start with "multipart/", Commons FileUpload's FileItemIteratorImpl throws InvalidContentTypeException whose message embeds the raw Content-Type header. No resource bundle contains the key struts.messages.upload.error.InvalidContentTypeException, so getDefaultMessage() falls back to that attacker-controlled default message and evaluates it as OGNL through TextParseUtil.translateVariables() -> OgnlTextParser.evaluate() -> ValueStack.findValue(). Attacker data therefore reaches an expression evaluator with no neutralization.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated OGNL injection through multipart Content-Type error handling
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage passes FileUploadException.getMessage() as the default localization message. LocalizedTextUtil then applies TextParseUtil.translateVariables to that default message, causing `$`/`%` OGNL expressions to be evaluated on the request ValueStack. Dispatcher.wrapRequest accepts any Content-Type containing multipart/form-data, so a malformed Content-Type reaches Commons FileUpload before action mapping; the FileUpload 1.3.1 rejection message includes the supplied header value and becomes the OGNL-capable message.

records.claim_title: BASIC authentication wrapper executes GET requests without credentials (auth bypass in openejb-http)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: BasicAuthHttpListenerWrapper.onMessage only fails closed for non-GET methods: the guard is `if (token != null || HttpRequest.Method.GET.name().equals(request.getMethod())) { httpListener.onMessage(...); }`. When the Authorization header is missing, malformed, or the credentials fail, `token` stays null but the wrapped listener is still invoked for every GET; the else branch is empty even though the comment says "login failed, return 401", so non-GET failures also return no 401. The wrapper is the only authentication gate for the standalone/embedded registries that use it.

records.claim_title: OS command injection through incomplete shell escaping of Commandline arguments/executable/working directory (BourneShell + Shell + StringUtils.quoteAndEscape)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Shell.getRawCommandLine (Shell.java:132-178) concatenates shell command, executable, working-directory preamble and arguments into one string that is executed as `/bin/sh -c <string>`. Arguments are passed through StringUtils.quoteAndEscape with only the single-quote character as an escape set and with a quoting-trigger list that omits newline; moreover quoteAndEscape short-circuits and returns the input unchanged when it merely starts and ends with the quote character (StringUtils.java:2314-2318), so an argument such as `''; <command>; ''` is emitted verbatim into the sh -c string. BourneShell (BourneShell.java:32-48, 55-69) also wraps the executable in double quotes while disabling both single- and double-quoted executable escaping (getEscapeChars returns an empty set, Shell.java:190-207), so `$`, backtick and `"` inside the executable remain active, and getExecutionPreamble/unifyQuotes (BourneShell.java:118-133, 157-170) interpolates the working directory with a fallback (StringUtils.escape) that leaves `$`, `;`, `&`, `|`, backtick and parentheses unescaped. Any shell command character that is neither in the trigger list nor in the escape set can therefore terminate/alter the intended command.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: AbstractSPARQLXMLParser.parseQueryResultInternal does not apply the parser's compulsory XML security features on the tuple-results path. The boolean path (lines 87-163) creates the XMLReader and then sets every setting returned by getCompulsoryXmlFeatureSettings() (SECURE_PROCESSING, DISALLOW_DOCTYPE_DECL=true, EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES=false, EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES=false, lines 278-285) plus the optional settings. records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultValidator.getValidDirectoryPath() enforces the "directory is inside parent" contract with `if (!dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath()))` (line 460). A string-prefix test is not a path-component containment test, so any sibling directory whose absolute path starts with the parent's absolute path string is accepted. The later check that the DirectoryName-validated canonical path equals the caller-supplied input (lines 465-469) does not repair this, because the sibling's canonical path does equal the input. The method then returns that out-of-parent path, and the public wrappers isValidDirectoryPath()/isValidFileUpload()/assertValidFileUpload() propagate the acceptance (isValidFileUpload is even documented to require the directory to be inside parent).

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: ESI include processing treats provider-supplied tag attributes as trusted URLs. Driver.render()/ResourceUtils.getHttpUrlWithQueryString() preserve absolute http/https URLs verbatim (ResourceUtils.java:67-74), DriverRequest marks them external (DriverRequest.java:54) and HttpClientRequestExecutor.createOutgoingRequest() connects to the physical host taken from the URL instead of rewriting it to the configured provider base (HttpClientRequestExecutor.java:227-241; UriUtils.isAbsolute only checks the http/https prefix, UriUtils.java:310-312). records.claim_title: Default XmlMapper/XmlFactory parses XML with an unhardened XMLInputFactory: DTD and external-entity processing are left enabled (XXE / entity-expansion)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XmlFactory, which is what the default XmlMapper constructor uses, creates the platform StAX parser with XMLInputFactory.newInstance() and then applies only one configuration setting, IS_COALESCING=true (XmlFactory.java:112-118, 136-142). It never disables DTD processing (XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD) or external general/parameter entity resolution (XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES), and it exposes no XML-specific read feature that could do so (FromXmlParser.Feature is empty, FromXmlParser.java:35-65). Parsing therefore inherits the defaults of whatever provider JAXP discovers; for the JDK's built-in StAX implementation those defaults permit DOCTYPE declarations and external entity resolution, so a DOCTYPE/entity in the document is expanded by the provider before Jackson converts events into tokens. A repo-wide search finds no occurrence of SUPPORT_DTD, exterior-entity properties, or any DTD/entity handling, so this is a missing secure-default rather than a code path that can be reached via configuration of the library itself.

records.claim_title: Default XmlFactory/XmlMapper leaves DTD processing and entity expansion enabled (incomplete XXE hardening)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XmlFactory's default configuration path only disables external-entity expansion on a self-created XMLInputFactory (`xmlIn.setProperty(XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES, Boolean.FALSE)`, XmlFactory.java:112-116) and never disables DTD processing (`XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD` is left at its Stax default of true; `IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES` is also never restricted). `_initFactories()` (XmlFactory.java:138-144) only sets IS_COALESCING. The Jackson XML layer does not compensate: XmlTokenStream consumes/ignores DTD-related Stax events (default branches of `_collectUntilTag()`/`_skipUntilTag()`, XmlTokenStream.java:350-388) and delegates all entity handling to the underlying Stax reader. The existing hardening is also path-dependent: it applies only when XmlFactory itself creates the factory, while `setXMLInputFactory()` (XmlFactory.java:342-344), the `XmlFactory(XMLInputFactory)` / `XmlMapper(XMLInputFactory)` constructors, and the JDK-deserialization path `readResolve()` (XmlFactory.java:184-204, which instantiates factories from stream-supplied class names and passes them to the constructor branch that skips the property) all bypass it.

records.claim_title: Unsigned `alg: none` JWT is accepted even when verifiers are supplied (signature verification bypass)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `JWTDecoder.decode(String, Verifier...)`, the two-part/no-signature handling at lines 70-76 is entered only when `verifiers.length == 0`. When verifiers ARE supplied, verifier selection (lines 79-84) leaves `verifier == null` for a header algorithm no supplied verifier supports — which is always the case for `Algorithm.none`, since HMACVerifier supports only HS* and RSAVerifier only RS*. The private `decode` then rejects an unsigned token only if a matching verifier was found (`parts.length == 2 && verifier != null`, line 164) and only requires a verifier for the three-part form (line 159). For a two-part token with `verifier == null`, both guards are false, the verification block at lines 168-172 is skipped, and the payload is deserialized and returned (lines 174-186). The same hole exists in the map-based overload (lines 125-142): an absent/unknown `kid` or an `alg` no map verifier supports yields `verifier == null`, again falling through to an unverified decode. This contradicts the in-source intent comments at line 69 ('if no verifiers were provided, decode if header says none, else throw an exception') and lines 163-164 ('A verifier was provided but no signature exists, this is treated as an invalid signature').

records.claim_title: JWT signature verification bypass for trailing-dot two-segment tokens in JWTDecoder
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `JWTDecoder.getParts` accepts a two-segment token when `encodedJWT.endsWith(".")` (lines 174-182), but the private `decode` gates both the missing-verifier check and the actual `verifier.verify()` call on `parts.length == 3` (lines 149-157). records.claim_title: Cross-site scripting in the JavaMelody monitoring reports via request-controlled values written into HTML/JavaScript without proper encoding (action message/anchor from `counter`, `graph` script block, X-Forwarded-For session address)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The HTML report writers embed values derived from HTTP requests in HTML attributes and JavaScript string/script contexts without context-appropriate escaping. `I18N.javascriptEncode` (javamelody-core/src/main/java/net/bull/javamelody/I18N.java:137-140) and its alias `urlEncode` (142-144) escape only backslash, newline, double and single quotes (not `<` or `/`), and `I18N.htmlEncode` (152-160) does not escape quotes. `HtmlCoreReport.writeMessageIfNotNull` (HtmlCoreReport.java:296-320) writes the action-result anchor directly into a JS single-quoted string with no encoding at all (lines 309-312), and the preceding `alert(...)` uses the bypassable `javascriptEncode` (line 301). The anchor/message are populated with the raw `counter` request parameter through `MonitoringController.executeActionIfNeeded` (MonitoringController.java:100-126, lines 108-119) and `Action.getContextName`/`Action.clearCounter` (Action.java:127-132 and 264-278). `Action.CLEAR_COUNTER` is explicitly excluded from `checkSystemActionsEnabled` (MonitoringController.java:109-111), and `collector.clearCounter` silently ignores unknown counter names (Collector.java:876-879), so an arbitrary payload is reflected into the page. Separately, `HtmlCounterReport.writeGraphDetailScript` (HtmlCounterReport.java:350-392, line 378) embeds the `graph` parameter through `urlEncode` inside a `<script>` block, so a `</script>` payload breaks out; and `HtmlSessionInformationsReport.writeSession` (HtmlSessionInformationsReport.java:158-163) writes the session remote address raw, which `MonitoringFilter.putUserInfoInSession` (MonitoringFilter.java:313-322) builds from the attacker-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` header (stored XSS on the sessions page).

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: CcmParser creates a Commons Digester and calls digester.parse(ccmXmlFile) after only setting validation off. records.claim_title: Method-pointer receiver expression is copied into the rewritten AST without transform(), leaving nested calls un-instrumented (sandbox interception bypass)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In SandboxTransformer.VisitorImpl.innerTransform (src/main/java/org/kohsuke/groovy/sandbox/SandboxTransformer.java:394-400), a MethodPointerExpression is rewritten to `new SandboxedMethodClosure(mpe.getExpression(), mpe.getMethodName())` using the original, untransformed child expressions. Unlike the other branches (e.g. CastExpression line 599, PropertyExpression lines 429/432, AttributeExpression 419/422, constructor/static-call arguments via transformArguments lines 290-304), the receiver sub-expression is never run through transform(). Because VisitorImpl.transform() returns the replacement node as soon as innerTransform matches (lines 311-318) and never lets the framework's default `super.transform(exp)`/exp.transformExpression(this) path process this node's children, any method call, property read, or constructor call embedded in the receiver expression is emitted into the transformed class as a plain call with no Checker.checked* wrapper. (The same omission pattern also exists for the dynamic method-name expression `arg1 = call.getMethod()` at line 360; treated here as the same root cause, not a second candidate.)

records.claim_title: Legacy descriptor endpoint doCheckRemote remains GET-reachable, bypassing the @RequirePOST guard on the credential-validation path (CSRF + SSRF + stored-credential use)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SubversionSCM.DescriptorImpl.doCheckRemote is a public Stapler web method that lacks the @RequirePOST annotation that every sibling credential-validation endpoint in this codebase carries. records.claim_title: Cleaner mutation XSS via `<noscript>` (parsed as markup by jsoup, as raw text by browsers with scripting enabled)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The HTML parser has no scripting flag: noscript content is always parsed as markup (HtmlTreeBuilderState.java:122-125 inserts noscript and switches to InHeadNoscript; InBody treats noscript as an ordinary element; HtmlTreeBuilder.java:76-77 documents 'if scripting enabled, rawtext'), whereas browsers with scripting enabled parse the same mark-up as RAWTEXT. The Cleaner (Cleaner.java:85-117) then copies whitelisted elements/attributes verbatim with only value-level escaping, and attribute serialization escapes '"' and '&' but deliberately leaves '<', '>' and '/' unescaped (Attribute.java:82-89 with Entities.java:120-131). The result is output in which a markup sequence that jsoup treated as an attribute value is reinterpreted by the browser as live markup once a whitelisted <noscript> wrapper puts it back into a raw-text context.

records.claim_title: XXE: APOC XML import procedures parse attacker-supplied XML with DTD/external-entity processing enabled (apoc.load.xml, apoc.load.xmlSimple, apoc.xml.import, apoc.import.graphml)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: APOC creates XML parsers with default, unsafe JAXP/StAX configuration and no EntityResolver/protocol allowlist. records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Java deserialization on the Neo4j Enterprise HA cluster coordination port (Netty ObjectDecoder on 0.0.0.0:5001-5099)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The cluster coordination transport serializes whole Java objects and installs org.jboss.netty.handler.codec.serialization.ObjectDecoder unconditionally on every accepted inbound connection. records.claim_title: Reflected XSS: request-derived exception messages are returned as text/html but only HTML-escaped for HTTP 400
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RESTEasy maps exception messages to response entities with Content-Type text/html for client errors (400 and 404) and for other failures, but the only built-in output-escaping control, MessageSanitizerContainerResponseFilter, runs exclusively when the response status equals 400 (HttpResponseCodes.SC_BAD_REQUEST). Therefore any message that reaches the client with a status other than 400 - in particular 404 NotFoundException messages - is emitted without HTML escaping. The message strings themselves are built from request data: ClassNode/SegmentNode build "Could not find resource for full path: " + request.getUri().getRequestUri(); SynchronousDispatcher builds "Unable to find JAX-RS resource associated with path: " + request.getUri().getPath() (the decoded path); PathParamInjector/QueryParamInjector/MatrixParamInjector rethrow StringParameterInjector conversion failures as NotFoundException (404) whose message embeds the parameter value, and three branches of StringParameterInjector.retrieveValue pass the raw decoded value (the other branches apply URLEncoder, showing the encoding was intended as a safeguard).

records.claim_title: Static-resource path validation gap allows traversal outside configured resource locations (ResourceHttpRequestHandler / PathResourceResolver / ResourceServlet)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Request-derived paths are validated as raw strings rather than as normalized/resolved paths. ResourceHttpRequestHandler.getResource() runs processPath()/isInvalidPath() on the path and then only a single URLDecoder.decode() re-check; the decoded value is not re-run through processPath()/isInvalidPath(), so control characters left inside path segments hide '..' from StringUtils.cleanPath() (e.g. a decoded segment such as '\u0000/../' is not recognized as '..' because the token is not exactly '..'), and the value actually used for resolution is always the un-normalized string. PathResourceResolver.isResourceUnderLocation() then accepts a resource using an un-normalized string prefix comparison (resource.getURL().getPath()/getPath() startsWith cleanPath(location) + '/'), and its percent-decoding check is skipped when the raw path contains no '%' and only looks for the literal '../' once. The same class of flaw exists in the deprecated ResourceServlet.doInclude(), which passes the user-supplied `resource` parameter straight to HttpServletRequest.getRequestDispatcher(url).include(...) with no path validation when allowedResources is not configured.

records.claim_title: Authentication bypass for accounts with null/empty stored password via default PlaintextPasswordEncoder in DaoAuthenticationProvider
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: PlaintextPasswordEncoder.isPasswordValid builds the stored side of the comparison as `String pass1 = encPass + "";`. If the stored password is null, Java string concatenation yields the four-character literal "null"; the presented side is `mergePasswordAndSalt(rawPass, salt, false)` and the two are compared with PasswordEncoderUtils.equals. An attacker who submits the password "null" therefore produces pass2 == "null" == pass1 and is authenticated. The same method also treats an empty stored password as matching an empty submitted password. DaoAuthenticationProvider selects this encoder by default (`setPasswordEncoder(new PlaintextPasswordEncoder())`, line 68) and passes `userDetails.getPassword()` straight into it (line 94), so the defect is on the default 4.2.x authentication path, not only in optional/deprecated configuration.

records.claim_title: AntPathRequestMatcher's default constructor matches case-sensitively despite its documented case-insensitive contract, weakening URL-based authorization rules
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In web/src/main/java/org/springframework/security/web/util/matcher/AntPathRequestMatcher.java, the two-argument constructor is documented as creating a matcher in a "case insensitive manner" (lines 78-85) but delegates with caseSensitive=true (line 87: `this(pattern, httpMethod, true);`). The one-argument constructor (line 74-76) funnels into the same path. Consequently every matcher created through these constructors performs case-sensitive comparison (SpringAntMatcher passes the flag to AntPathMatcher.setCaseSensitive, lines 288-293; SubpathMatcher lowercases paths only when !caseSensitive, lines 306-317), contradicting the documented semantics and the pattern used by the sibling RegexRequestMatcher whose code and javadoc agree. This class is the default matcher behind all `antMatchers(...)` URL authorization rules (config/.../AbstractRequestMatcherRegistry.java lines 257-265), `HttpSecurity.antMatcher(...)` (config/.../builders/HttpSecurity.java lines 1325-1327), and login/logout processing-URL matchers (FormLoginConfigurer line 249, LogoutConfigurer lines 346-353, OAuth2LoginConfigurer line 474, OpenIDLoginConfigurer line 288).

records.claim_title: Untrusted OAuth2 scope names are embedded in the SpEL-evaluated whitelabel approval page (reflected XSS / expression injection)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint builds the approval page by string concatenation: each scope name obtained from the request/approval model is substituted raw into the HTML template (WhitelabelApprovalEndpoint.createScopes lines 46-60, templates at lines 66-72), and the resulting string is handed to SpelView, which scans it for `${...}` placeholders and parses/evaluates each placeholder name as a SpEL expression against a StandardEvaluationContext with MapAccessor (SpelView lines 39-58 and 64-74). Because the untrusted scope text is concatenated into the template BEFORE the SpEL pass and is never escaped or restricted, attacker-controlled text can (a) inject HTML/JavaScript into the approval page and (b) inject SpEL expressions that are evaluated server-side with default StandardEvaluationContext capabilities (type references such as T(...) and method invocation).

records.claim_title: @Path parameter values are neither encoded for '.'/'..' nor validated, allowing request-path traversal / endpoint confusion
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Retrofit 2.4.x inserts `@Path` values into the endpoint's relative URL with `relativeUrl.replace("{" + name + "}", canonicalizeForPath(value, encoded))` (RequestBuilder.java:89-95). `canonicalizeForPath` (RequestBuilder.java:97-144) percent-encodes only C0/non-ASCII characters, the always-encode set `" \"<>^`{}|\\?#"` (line 33), and `/`/`%` when `alreadyEncoded == false` (lines 103,127). The `.` character is never encoded, and there is no check rejecting `.`/`..`/`%2e` segments before the relative URL is resolved against the base URL in `RequestBuilder.get()` (lines 189-202) / `addQueryParam()` (lines 146-164). OkHttp's `HttpUrl.resolve`/`newBuilder` normalizes dot segments, so the value can change the path structure of the final request. The @Path Javadoc still promises values are 'URL encoded' and used as a 'Named replacement in a URL path segment' (Path.java:28-40), so the contract is broken by dot segments.

records.claim_title: Unvalidated external-reference resolution: SSRF, local file read, and credential disclosure to attacker-chosen URLs
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Spec content is trusted for resource locations. `$ref` strings (and legacy resource-listing paths) are split/joined and passed directly to network/file loaders with no protocol, host, or directory-containment validation: `ResolverCache.loadRef` (ResolverCache.java:110-118) hands the attacker-supplied file/URL portion to `RefUtils.readExternalRef`/`readExternalUrlRef`; the URL branch calls `RemoteUrl.urlToString` (RefUtils.java:59, 127), which does `new URL(cleanUrl(url))` and `openConnection()` for any JDK-supported scheme/host (RemoteUrl.java:98, 124, 133); the relative branch does `parentDirectory.resolve(file).normalize()` (RefUtils.java:130) with no check that the result stays under `parentDirectory`, so absolute paths and `../` escapes are read via FileInputStream (RefUtils.java:133) or the classpath (RefUtils.java:135). Additionally, when the root location is remote, `ResolverCache` passes `parentDirectory == null` (ResolverCache.java:64-73) and relative URLs are rebuilt and fetched (RefUtils.java:74-114). `RemoteUrl.urlToString` then applies every plain (non-`ManagedValue`) `AuthorizationValue` as a header or query parameter to whatever URL is being fetched (RemoteUrl.java:101-109, 127-129), i.e. to attacker-selected hosts as well. The legacy converter repeats the pattern: `SwaggerCompatConverter.read` builds a fetch location from the attacker-controlled `ApiListingReference.getPath()` (SwaggerCompatConverter.java:135-169) and `readDeclaration` fetches it via `RemoteUrl.urlToString` (SwaggerCompatConverter.java:487).

records.claim_title: Internal blacklist for known gadget types is inert on default XStream instances (insecureWarning cleared before unmarshalling)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XStream.InternalBlackList.canConvert() only rejects java.beans.EventHandler, any class whose name ends with "$LazyIterator", and javax.crypto.* types when the private field `insecureWarning` is true (XStream.java:2539-2546). However, XStream.unmarshal(...) sets `insecureWarning = false` before delegating to the actual unmarshalling strategy (XStream.java:1482-1486), and the converter lookup (which calls canConvert) happens inside that strategy. Consequently the flag is always false when the blacklist is evaluated during any unmarshal, so only the unconditional `void`/`Void` check can ever fire; the security-relevant type checks are unreachable in the unmarshalling path. Because the internal blacklist is the compensating control for the default, uninitialized security framework (setupSecurity() grants AnyTypePermission.ANY and sets insecureWarning = true, XStream.java:693-700; blacklist registered at PRIORITY_LOW, ahead of ReflectionConverter at PRIORITY_VERY_LOW, XStream.java:957-964), the documented protection is silently lost.

records.claim_title: Unescaped `like`/`notLike` pattern concatenated into HQL/JPQL (query injection)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: LikeCondition.createQueryFragment builds the predicate as `selector + " " + getLike() + " '" + type.wrap(toMatch) + "' "` (lines 86-89). Type.wrap (lines 32-58) only prefixes/appends `%` and performs no single-quote escaping, and LikeCondition.getParameters() returns Collections.emptyList() (lines 103-106), so the pattern is never bound as a JPA parameter. In contrast, eq/neq/lt/lte/gt/gte/in/notIn/between all call selector.generateParameter(value), producing a `:name` placeholder (ValueParameter, lines 51-57) that DefaultQueryBuilder.createJPAQuery binds via query.setParameter (lines 430-434). The like value is the sole predicate value interpolated directly into the HQL/JPQL text.

records.claim_title: Open redirect via unvalidated `redirectedFrom` parameter in AppointmentBlockFormController
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: AppointmentBlockFormController.onSubmit accepts the request parameter `redirectedFrom` (line 157) and uses it directly to build the Spring view name `"redirect:" + redirectedFrom` at line 313, with no whitelist or validation. records.claim_title: Unsafe SnakeYAML deserialization in Yaml/Dynamics YAML parsing APIs (snakeyaml 1.28, non-safe Constructor)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: io.kubernetes.client.util.Yaml binds YAML to Kubernetes models through `CustomConstructor extends org.yaml.snakeyaml.constructor.Constructor` (Yaml.java:219-234) and exposes it via `getSnakeYaml()` -> `new org.yaml.snakeyaml.Yaml(new CustomConstructor(), new CustomRepresenter())` (Yaml.java:359-362). `Constructor`/its subclasses honor YAML global tags and instantiate arbitrary classes via Class.forName + bean property/constructor handling; snakeyaml 1.28 (pom.xml:43, dependencyManagement pom.xml:100-104, used in util/pom.xml:33-36) predates the 2.0 default restriction. `io.kubernetes.client.util.generic.dynamic.Dynamics` is worse and uses the raw unsafe default `new Yaml()` (Dynamics.java:24) and calls `yamlCodec.load(yamlContent)` (Dynamics.java:62-64). There is no tag whitelist, no SafeConstructor/TrustedPrefixes filtering and no documented 'trusted input only' contract on these public APIs, so YAML-level tags (`!!...`) reach class loading/instantiation in the client JVM.

records.claim_title: Directory containment bypass in FileSecurityUtils.isFileOutsideDir due to raw prefix comparison of canonical paths
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: isFileOutsideDir returns !file.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(baseDir.getCanonicalPath()). String.startsWith performs a character-prefix test with no requirement that the following character be a path separator (or end of string). Any sibling path whose absolute name begins with the base directory string is therefore classified as inside the base directory. Canonicalization correctly resolves '.'/'..' and symlinks, but it cannot compensate for the missing separator boundary; there is also no case-normalization for case-insensitive filesystems.

records.claim_title: Unvalidated CDATA-section content is passed through the SAX scanner and emitted as a CDATA section (mXSS/policy bypass)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In the SAX path the NekoHTML parser is configured with the cdata-sections feature enabled (AntiSamySAXScanner.getParser(), line 209), so `<![CDATA[ ... ]]>` in the attacker input is reported as a CDATA section. MagicSAXFilter.characters() (lines 97-115) handles that case by computing an HTML-entity-encoded copy of the text *only for the error message* and then unconditionally forwarding the raw, unmodified `text` to super.characters(), i.e. into the XSLT/serializer pipeline. Because the parser reports the CDATA body as character data, its contents are never dispatched as startElement/endElement/attribute events and therefore are never checked against the AntiSamy policy. The serializer keeps CDATA sections in its output (BaseMarkupSerializer.startCDATA/endCDATA behavior is relied upon by ASHTMLSerializer.endElementIO, lines 51-53, which prints `]]>` when `state.inCData`; the comment there even notes CDATA is 'Illegal in HTML, but still' emitted). The DOM scanner implements the opposite, safe behavior for the same construct: recursiveValidateTag() detects `Text` nodes of type CDATA_SECTION_NODE and calls stripCData() (lines 254-257, 649-654), which replaces the CDATA node with an ordinary text node whose content is escaped on serialization.

records.claim_title: Windows command-line construction does not neutralize cmd.exe metacharacters when the line is dispatched to cmd.exe (batch/cmd targets)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: WindowsProcess.getCommandLine() joins every element of the caller-supplied command list via WindowsCreateProcessEscape.quote() and passes the single resulting string to CreateProcessW (lpApplicationName = NULL), without any cmd.exe-aware escaping or command/argument validation. quote()/mightNeedQuotes() only handle the MSVC/CRT tokenizer (space, tab, double quote, backslash runs), so shell metacharacters that cmd.exe interprets (&, |, ^, <, >, and % / ! expansion) are emitted verbatim. Windows implicitly executes .bat/.cmd targets through cmd.exe /c, so an attacker-influenced argument crosses from data into cmd.exe command syntax.

records.claim_title: Controller-side URL fetch (blind SSRF / unbounded read) when configuring or using a ClasspathEntry
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: ClasspathEntry accepts any URL (ClasspathEntry.pathToURL, lines 68-82) and the approval check hashes the entry by fully reading it from the URL (ScriptApproval.Hasher.hashClasspathEntry, lines 229-242, called from checkAndConvertApprovedClasspath, lines 315-336). ScriptApproval.configuring(ClasspathEntry, ApprovalContext) (lines 652-694) invokes that check when a configuration is saved, and ScriptApproval.using(ClasspathEntry) (lines 724-744) does so on every evaluation; SecureGroovyScript.configuring (lines 146-155) and SecureGroovyScript.evaluate (lines 402-418) drive these calls. There is no allowlist of URL schemes/hosts and no connect/read timeout, so a user able to configure a script with classpath entries can force the controller to issue GETs to arbitrary internal URLs (or read arbitrary absolute local files, which are discarded after hashing) even if the entry is never approved.

records.claim_title: SYSTEM-scoped Kubernetes credentials are returned to item-level lookups because getCredentials ignores itemGroup and credential scope
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: KubernetesCredentialProvider.getCredentials(Class<C>, ItemGroup, Authentication) (lines 208-227) returns all credentials stored in its map whenever `ACL.SYSTEM.equals(authentication)` is true; the `itemGroup` parameter is accepted but never used and the credential's CredentialsScope is never inspected. The plugin nevertheless implements scope: SecretUtils.getCredentialScope() (SecretUtils.java lines 106-123) parses the `jenkins.io/credentials-scope` label and every converter stamps that scope onto the produced credential (e.g. UsernamePasswordCredentialsConvertor.java line 56, StringCredentialConvertor.java line 54), and docs/examples/README.md line 13 documents `global`/`system` as the supported scopes. The `system` value therefore only has meaning if the provider excludes such credentials when credentials are requested for a non-null item group, which this implementation does not do.
