records.claim_title: Open redirect in DefaultLogoutLogic via protocol-relative URL that matches the default logout URL pattern
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultLogoutLogic takes the attacker-controlled request parameter `url` and, if it matches the configured logout URL pattern, passes it unmodified to HttpAction.redirect (Location header). The default pattern used when none is configured is Pac4jConstants.DEFAULT_LOGOUT_URL_PATTERN_VALUE = "/.*", which requires only that the value start with '/'. A protocol-relative URL such as `//attacker.example` therefore fully matches the pattern even though the constant is documented as meaning "only relative urls are allowed", and `Location: //attacker.example` is resolved by browsers as an absolute URL to the attacker's host.

records.claim_title: Default XStream blacklist omits command-execution gadget classes (java.lang.ProcessBuilder, javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter), enabling RCE via crafted XML under the uninitialized security framework
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XStream.setupSecurity() (XStream.java 639-649) grants AnyTypePermission.ANY and adds only denyTypes(new String[]{"java.beans.EventHandler"}) plus the LAZY_ITERATORS and JAVAX_CRYPTO regexes. records.claim_title: Job id elements containing '..' traverse out of the job status storage (arbitrary directory deletion / out-of-store file write, read and log creation)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultJobStatusStore encodes each job id element with URLEncoder.encode(name, "UTF-8") (line 214), which leaves '.' untouched, and getJobFolder() then builds the folder with new File(folder, encode(idElement)) (line 347) without any traversal check. An id element exactly equal to '..' therefore resolves to the parent of the configured store root (JobManagerConfiguration.getStorage() = <permanent-dir>/jobs/status). The resulting folder is used destructively/creatively: remove() calls FileUtils.deleteDirectory(jobFolder) on it (line 459), saveJobStatus() writes status.xml.zip into it after file.mkdirs() (lines 368-373 and JobStatusSerializer.write lines 91-94), loadStatus() reads status.xml[.zip] from it (lines 285-323) and createLoggerTail() creates log files next to it (lines 354-357, 471-488). The same repository hardens the analogous case in PathUtils.encode() (extension module, line 56: .replace(".", "%2E")), so the missing dot-encoding in the job store is an asymmetry rather than an intrinsic requirement.

records.claim_title: Unbounded recursion in UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS handling (primitive value deserializers and BuilderBasedDeserializer) allows stack exhaustion / denial of service
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: When `DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS` is enabled, the unwrap branch consumes one `START_ARRAY` (`p.nextToken()`) and then re-invokes the same deserialization routine on whatever follows it, without validating that the following token is not itself another `START_ARRAY`. The check that the maintainers use elsewhere is absent here: `StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue` (lines 355-369) explicitly fails when the current token is `START_ARRAY`, and `BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray` (lines 631-645, comment dated 23-Aug-2022) explicitly rejects a second nested array. Because the recursive call happens before any end-of-array validation (`_verifyEndArrayForSingle` runs only after the nested call returns), recursion depth is exactly the attacker-supplied JSON array nesting depth, with no limit anywhere in the library (no depth counter, no `getNestingDepth`, no `StreamReadConstraints` in this snapshot).

records.claim_title: Unbounded gzip decompression write into fixed 3x scratch buffer in Utility.decode (out-of-bounds array write)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Utility.decode(String, boolean) allocates the decompression buffer from the compressed size, not the decompressed size: `final byte[] tmp = new byte[bytes.length * 3];` (Utility.java:658) and then copies every decoded byte with an unchecked array store `tmp[count++] = (byte) b;` (Utility.java:662). records.claim_title: Path traversal in admin REST log viewer allows arbitrary file read
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The admin REST resource StructuredLogViewerResource.getRecords() binds the request query parameter `logFileName` (line 90) to a String and forwards it, via getWithType(), to LogFilter.getLogRecordsUsingQuery() (LogFilter.java lines 142-216). For the DAS branch, LogFilter builds the target path by string concatenation: `logFileDetailsForServer.substring(0, lastIndexOf(File.separator)) + File.separator + logFileName.trim()` (lines 167-168). The only guard is `new File(logFileName).exists()` (line 169); there is no normalization, no canonical-path containment check, and no whitelist of allowed log file names, so `../` sequences (or absolute-path tricks handled by getLogFile(), lines 637-652) escape the logs directory. The resolved file is then wrapped in LogFile (getLogFile -> new LogFile(fileName)) and read in LogFile.getLogEntries() (LogFile.java lines 102-155). LogParserFactory.createLogParser() selects RawLogParser for unrecognized content (LogParserFactory.java lines 102-109), and RawLogParser.parseLog() puts every line of the file into ParsedLogRecord.LOG_MESSAGE (RawLogParser.java lines 66-71), so the whole file is emitted as log records and returned to the requester in the JSON/XML LogRecordList (StructuredLogViewerResource.convertQueryResult, lines 162-198). The same concatenation flaw exists on the non-DAS/instance branch (LogFilter.java lines 394-408) and the admin console UI passes the same request-controlled value through without validation (LogViewHandlers.getLogQueryAttributes, lines 106 and 210).

records.claim_title: Path traversal via NiFi Registry extension-bundle coordinates allows writes and recursive deletion outside the bundle storage directory
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: NAR MANIFEST attributes Nar-Group/Nar-Id/Nar-Version are stored as the bundle's groupId/artifactId/version with only non-blank validation (BundleIdentifier.validateNotBlank, Bundle @NotBlank, BundleVersionMetadata @NotBlank). FileSystemBundlePersistenceProvider builds filesystem paths by concatenating sanitize(bucketId)+"/"+sanitize(groupId)+"/"+sanitize(artifactId)[+"/"+sanitize(version)] and resolving with new File(storage, ...). sanitize() only delegates to FileUtils.sanitizeFilename (replaces /, \, control chars, : * ? " < > | and space) plus trim/lowercase, so a value of ".." is passed through unchanged. records.claim_root_cause_or_alert:
In DefaultHTMLCleaner, script and style content is explicitly kept as CDATA (setUseCdataForScriptAndStyle(true), setOmitCdataOutsideScriptAndStyle(true)) and in restricted mode the elements are only renamed to 
 (TagTransformation(script->pre), TagTransformation(style->pre)) without escaping their content. HTMLUtils.toString() then serializes the DOM through JDOM and its XWikiXMLOutputter prints CDATA sections verbatim (no printCDATA/escaping override) and additionally un-escapes '&#NNN;' sequences (cleanAmpersandEscape). records.claim_title: @SafeHtml whitelist bypass: constraint delegates its verdict to jsoup Cleaner.isValid() on a rebuilt XML-parsed document (jsoup pinned at 1.8.3), allowing XSS payloads to validate
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SafeHtmlValidator.isValid(CharSequence, ConstraintValidatorContext) does not sanitize the value or compare the value with a sanitized equivalent; it returns `new Cleaner( whitelist ).isValid( getFragmentAsDocument( value ) )` (SafeHtmlValidator.java:80). getFragmentAsDocument (lines 86-100) parses the raw value with `Parser.xmlParser()`, then copies only `fragment.children()` (element children; top-level text and comments are silently dropped) into a brand-new shell document, so the verdict is taken on a *reconstructed* document, not on the user's string, and the raw string is left unchanged for the application to render. In addition, the build pins jsoup to 1.8.3 (pom.xml:136, engine/pom.xml:91-94, optional dependency, aligned with the supported WildFly), a 2014 release whose `Cleaner.isValid()` only determines whether cleaning retained the same number of top-level nodes and does not detect attributes removed by the whitelist (the 'discarded attributes' accounting was added in later jsoup releases). Any whitelist violation that does not change the top-level element count, or any difference between the XML parse used for validation and the browser's HTML parse of the rendered string, therefore yields 'valid' and the constraint's security guarantee is void.

records.claim_title: Unbounded MIME part header parsing in AttachmentDeserializer enables remote memory-exhaustion DoS
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: core/src/main/java/org/apache/cxf/attachment/AttachmentDeserializer.java parses MIME part headers via loadPartHeaders() -> readLine(), appending every attacker byte up to '\n' into a StringBuilder (no maximum length or cumulative byte counter), and loadPartHeaders() also accumulates header-continuation lines without bound before storing them in a TreeMap. No size limit exists anywhere in the class; only attachment *content* is bounded, and only when the optional ATTACHMENT_MAX_SIZE / ATTACHMENT_MEMORY_THRESHOLD properties are configured (applied via AttachmentUtil.setStreamedAttachmentProperties to CachedOutputStream, not to headers). records.claim_title: HTTP/1.x request framing desync (request smuggling) from lenient Content-Length / Transfer-Encoding header parsing
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: HttpObjectDecoder parses HTTP/1 headers permissively and never normalizes/rejects ambiguous framing headers. splitHeader() stops the name at whitespace and then searches forward for a colon, so whitespace before the colon (or leading whitespace on the first header line) is silently accepted and the header is treated as valid (HttpObjectDecoder.java:716-747, plus the obs-fold branch at 572-586). readHeaders() chooses body framing without rejecting ambiguity: it stores every Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding header as-is (572-598) and prefers chunked TE over CL (604-615). contentLength() (618-623) delegates to HttpUtil.getContentLength(message, -1L), which returns only the first Content-Length value and does no duplicate/conflicting-value check (HttpUtil.java:147-189). The strict helpers that later Netty versions use here (e.g. HttpUtil.normalizeAndGetContentLength and duplicate/last-wins Content-Length rejection) do not exist in this snapshot (searches for 'normalize' in codec-http and 'Multiple Content-Length' return no matches), and no post-2019 security fixes are present in this file.

records.claim_title: OpenSslEngine SSLSession returns certificate issuer instead of subject as peer/local principal
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In the OpenSslSession implementation, the helper `principal(Certificate[] certs)` calls `((java.security.cert.X509Certificate) certs[0]).getIssuerX500Principal()`; it should return the certificate subject (`getSubjectX500Principal()`). `getPeerPrincipal()` and `getLocalPrincipal()` therefore expose the certificate's issuer DN as the session principal. In the OpenSslSession implementation, the helper `principal(Certificate[] certs)` calls `((java.security.cert.X509Certificate) certs[0]).getIssuerX500Principal()`; it should return the certificate subject (`getSubjectX500Principal()`). `getPeerPrincipal()` and `getLocalPrincipal()` therefore expose the certificate's issuer DN as the session principal. The JDK-provider path (`JdkSslSession`) delegates to the JDK `SSLSession`, which returns the subject principal, so the two SSL providers disagree on the same handshake.
records.rationale: 원본 수정은 HTTP cookie codec을 RFC6265 strict/lax API로 교체해 cookie 값 검증을 강화하는 것인데, 응답은 OpenSslEngine이 인증서 subject 대신 issuer를 principal로 돌려주는 별도 문제를 지목했다.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The getACL request case in FinalRequestProcessor (lines 366-377) deserializes GetACLRequest and returns zks.getZKDatabase().getACL(path, stat) directly. records.claim_title: HTTP/1 request smuggling via inconsistent Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length framing in HttpObjectDecoder
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The HTTP/1.1 decoder accepts ambiguous message-framing headers and resolves them locally instead of rejecting them, so it can disagree with an intermediary about where the body ends. (1) `HttpObjectDecoder.readHeaders()` (lines 603-615) picks the body state: if `HttpUtil.isTransferEncodingChunked(message)` is true it reads chunked, else if `contentLength() >= 0` it reads a fixed-length body, and the message is forwarded with BOTH headers still present (nothing removes Content-Length). (2) `HttpUtil.isTransferEncodingChunked()` (lines 303-305) calls `message.headers().contains(TRANSFER_ENCODING, CHUNKED, true)`, which dispatches to `DefaultHttpHeaders.contains(CharSequence,CharSequence,boolean)` -> `DefaultHeaders.contains(name,value,CASE_INSENSITIVE_HASHER)` (DefaultHeaders lines 249-262) comparing the *entire* header value with `AsciiString.contentEqualsIgnoreCase` (AsciiString lines 1359-1370). Only a header line that is exactly `chunked` is recognized; a comma-separated value that per RFC 7230 §3.3.3 establishes chunked framing (`Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked`) is treated as NOT chunked, while a proxy decodes the chunked body. Combined with a Content-Length header the decoder then uses the Content-Length boundary (line 610-611), producing a front-end/back-end desync (TE.CL). Conversely, when TE is exactly `chunked` and a Content-Length is also present, Netty reads chunked (line 608-609) while a proxy using the Content-Length frames differently (CL.TE); the conflicting Content-Length is never removed from the decoded message. (3) `HttpUtil.getContentLength(HttpMessage, long)` (lines 174-179) reads only the last `Content-Length` value (`DefaultHeaders.get()` loops and overwrites, lines 111-128) and never checks for duplicates or conflicting values, so `Content-Length: 6` + `Content-Length: 0` is resolved silently in Netty's favor.

records.claim_title: camel-rabbitmq consumer deserializes sender-controlled Java object bodies without any allow-list/opt-out (CWE-502)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RabbitMQMessageConverter.populateMessageBody() unconditionally calls deserializeBody() when the incoming AMQP message carries the header CamelSerialize=true, and deserializeBody() performs `new ObjectInputStream(byteArrayInputStream).readObject()` on the raw broker delivery body. The trigger flag is part of the message properties supplied by whichever client published the message, and this snapshot exposes no endpoint/component option to disable Java deserialization or restrict the classes that may be instantiated (no allowJavaSerializedMessage / trustedPackages-style guard; verified absent by repository-wide search). The consumer therefore treats an untrusted broker publisher as authoritative for a Java-deserialization decision.

records.claim_title: HTTP/1 decoder does not reconcile Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding, enabling request smuggling
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Body-length framing for HTTP/1 messages is decided from raw header values without normalization or cross-header validation. (1) HttpUtil.isTransferEncodingChunked() uses HttpHeaders.contains(name, value, ignoreCase), which compares a whole header value and does not split on commas (HttpHeaders.contains(String,String,boolean), lines 1106-1122), unlike containsValue() which explicitly handles comma-separated lists (lines 1124-1142). Therefore 'Transfer-Encoding: gzip, chunked' (valid, chunked final) is not detected as chunked. (2) HttpObjectDecoder.readHeaders() then selects READ_FIXED_LENGTH_CONTENT/VARIABLE_LENGTH_CONTENT instead of READ_CHUNK_SIZE (lines 603-615). (3) For a request with no parseable Content-Length, contentLength() is -1 and decode() emits the message plus EMPTY_LAST_CONTENT and resets (lines 241-247), so subsequent bytes are parsed as the next request. (4) HttpUtil.getContentLength() reads only one of possibly multiple Content-Length values (lines 174-189) and keeps Content-Length when Transfer-Encoding: chunked applies, so conflicting duplicates are also accepted.

records.claim_title: XXE: pooled SAX parsers are built without DTD/external-entity restrictions or an ignoring EntityResolver; attacker-supplied XLSX/XML can trigger external entity resolution
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParserFactory() enables only XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and never disables DOCTYPE processing, external general/parameter entities, or external DTD loading. XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParser()/parseSAX() then hand out pooled javax.xml.parsers.SAXParser instances and call parser.parse(is, handler) without installing the IGNORING_SAX_ENTITY_RESOLVER that getXMLReader() sets (XMLReaderUtils.java:92-96,117-126,142-152,333-344). ParseContext.getSAXParserFactory() has the identical gap (ParseContext.java:148-168). Because javax.xml.parsers.SAXParser.parse(InputStream, DefaultHandler) registers the passed DefaultHandler as ContentHandler/EntityResolver/DTDHandler/ErrorHandler, protection is accidental: it only exists when the caller wraps its handler in OfflineContentHandler (whose resolveEntity returns an empty stream). The XSSF worksheet path does not: XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet() calls XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX(sheetInputStream, handler, parseContext) with XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer, which extends DefaultHandler and does not override resolveEntity (returns null → parser default resolution), while the sheet XML comes from the attacker-supplied XLSX package. NetworkParser/TeeContentHandler has the same property (CLI --network only).

records.claim_title: OS command injection through unquoted user name in shell-based group mapping (bash -c "id -Gn " + user)

records.claim_title: CSRF protection scope mismatch: privileged state-changing endpoints are reachable via GET (and via crumb-exempt multipart POSTs), so ambient-session requests can run scripts / shut down / disable nodes
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `hudson.security.csrf.CrumbFilter` enforces the crumb only for requests whose method is exactly `POST` (line 55) and additionally exempts multipart bodies (`if (valid || isMultipart(httpRequest))`, line 84) with the comment that multipart requests "need to be handled by each handler". Several privileged handlers therefore rely on protection that never runs for them: they neither declare `@RequirePOST` nor test `req.getMethod()`, so a plain GET executes them. This is inconsistent with the surrounding code, where comparable endpoints carry `@RequirePOST` (e.g. AbstractItem.doDoDelete:481-483, AbstractProject.doDoDelete:1874-1876, Run.doDoDelete:1951-1952, View.doDoDelete:949-950, User.doDoDelete:542-543, Job/View/Computer doConfigSubmit, AbstractProject.doDisable/doEnable:2009-2021), and `Jenkins.doRestart`/`doSafeRestart` (3182-3206) explicitly branch on `req.getMethod().equals("GET")` to show a confirmation page first. The omissions are thus individual gaps, not a deliberate "GET is fine" design.

records.claim_title: Multipart upload error path feeds attacker-controlled request data into OGNL evaluation via the localized error message (expression-language injection → potential RCE)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Multipart parse failures are converted into user-visible messages by passing the *raw exception message* as the default message of LocalizedTextUtil.findText (see buildErrorMessage). LocalizedTextUtil then unconditionally runs TextParseUtil.translateVariables(...) over that default text, i.e. anything of the form %{...} or ${...} in it is compiled and executed as an OGNL expression against the action value stack. Because the request's Content-Type / multipart metadata is echoed by Commons FileUpload into its exception messages (e.g. InvalidContentTypeException '...content type header is <value>'), attacker text reaches expression evaluation. The message bundle only defines two generic keys (SizeLimitExceededException, IOException), so for all other exception types the attacker-influenced default-message fallback is used. The framework relies on message *arguments* (safe) in some places but the fallback path puts untrusted text directly into the message *template*.

records.claim_title: Unfiltered Java deserialization of management HTTP request bodies allows RCE on the manager/locator (legacy gfsh HTTP API)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The management web application registers SerializableObjectHttpMessageConverter (geode-mgmt-servlet.xml:51). Its readInternal() deserializes the raw HTTP body for any Serializable-typed @RequestBody parameter using IOUtils.deserializeObject(bytes, classLoader) (SerializableObjectHttpMessageConverter:63-75). IOUtils.deserializeObject wraps the attacker bytes in ClassLoaderObjectInputStream, a subclass of java.io.ObjectInputStream that calls readObject() without ever installing an ObjectInputFilter or class allow-list (IOUtils:163-174, 332-357). The project's hardening hook (InternalDataSerializer.initialize / ObjectInputStreamFilterWrapper, driven by validate-serializable-objects + serializable-object-filter) is applied only to Geode DataSerializer streams and is never invoked here, so even a hardened cluster remains exposed. No controller-level authorization exists on the reachable endpoint: ShellCommandsController.queryNames is annotated only with @RequestMapping (no @PreAuthorize like geode-web-api), and the servlet's only interceptor, LoginHandlerInterceptor.preHandle, authenticates (securityService.login) but never authorizes. Because argument resolution (body deserialization) happens after preHandle but before the handler method executes, the gadget's readObject() runs before any Geode permission check, and an account with no cluster permissions is sufficient when integrated security is enabled; when no SecurityManager is configured (the default) no credentials are needed at all.

records.claim_title: XStreamer.fromXML rebuilds an attacker-controlled XStream (permissions + converters) from the same untrusted document, defeating the type-permission whitelist
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XStreamer.fromXML(driver, Reader, TypePermission...) creates an `outer` XStream that is restricted by the caller-supplied/default permissions (XStreamer.PERMISSIONS, XStreamer.java:54-64, 261-266), reads an embedded `com.thoughtworks.xstream.XStream` instance out of the same untrusted XML (XStreamer.java:268), and then immediately uses that attacker-reconstructed instance to deserialize the rest of the document (XStreamer.java:269-273). The reconstructed instance carries attacker-chosen state including its SecurityMapper permission list and its converter registry, and the only permission check performed while reading that state is against the *outer* permission set, which by design allows XStream's own configuration types (TypeHierarchyPermission(TypePermission.class), Mapper, XStream, WildcardTypePermission on the com.thoughtworks.xstream package, XStreamer.java:54-64). Consequently the payload after the embedded configuration is deserialized under the attacker's policy, not the application's.

records.claim_title: BC JSSE client never enforces endpoint identification (hostname verification)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The BCJSSE provider accepts and stores SSLParameters.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm() in ProvSSLParameters, but nothing in the handshake consults it. Certificate validation for clients is performed only through TlsAuthentication.notifyServerCertificate -> ProvTlsManager.isServerTrusted(chain, authType), which calls the 2-argument X509TrustManager.checkServerTrusted(chain, authType) in ProvSSLSocketDirect, ProvSSLEngine and ProvSSLSocketWrap. Neither the socket/engine overloads nor the provider's own trust-manager implementation (ProvX509TrustManagerImpl) ever compare the peer host with the certificate identities; ProvX509ExtendedTrustManager_7 simply forwards socket/engine overloads back to the same non-verifying 2-argument path. The only hostname matching code in the tree (JsseDefaultHostnameAuthorizer) belongs to the separate EST client and is not used by BCJSSE.

records.claim_title: TLS hostname verification silently skipped for `ssl=true` (and for verify-full with a custom sslfactory), allowing server impersonation/MITM
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MakeSSL.convert decides whether to verify the server certificate identity from the raw `sslmode` property value (`"verify-full".equals(sslmode)`) and from `factory instanceof LibPQFactory` (lines 88-98), instead of the driver's SslMode model. `SslMode.of()` (SslMode.java lines 63-71) explicitly maps the legacy `ssl` property to VERIFY_FULL, and ssl-client.md promises server identity validation that prevents man-in-the-middle attacks, but the connection path never uses SslMode.of()/verifyPeerName(). Consequently: (1) with `ssl=true` and no `sslmode`, the property is null, so MakeSSL picks `SSLSocketFactory.getDefault()` (line 44) and the verification block is skipped entirely (line 89 is false); (2) even with `sslmode=verify-full`, a user-supplied `sslfactory` makes `factory instanceof LibPQFactory` false, so no hostname check is performed. The only code that ever verifies the hostname is `org.postgresql.ssl.jdbc4.LibPQFactory.verify()` (lines 281-328), reachable only in the first configuration. Standard JSSE `SSLSocketFactory`/`SSLSocket` validate the chain against the default trust store but do not perform endpoint/hostname identification unless explicitly configured, which this code does not do.

records.claim_title: Missing OfflineContentHandler when SAX-parsing XLSX worksheet XML enables XML External Entity (XXE) processing of attacker-supplied spreadsheets
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX(InputStream, DefaultHandler, ParseContext) relies on the top-level DefaultHandler passed by the caller to act as the SAX EntityResolver (SAXParser.parse(InputStream, DefaultHandler) registers that handler as ContentHandler/EntityResolver). Tika's XXE guard is OfflineContentHandler, whose resolveEntity() returns an empty stream and which must therefore be the outermost handler. In XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet (line 342) the handler object XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer (extends org.xml.sax.helpers.DefaultHandler, which inherits DefaultHandler.resolveEntity returning null) is passed directly, so Xerces falls back to default (external) entity resolution for the worksheet XML. Every comparable call site in the tree wraps the handler, e.g. the same class wraps workbook data at line 200 ('new OfflineContentHandler(new AbsPathExtractorHandler())'), and other OOXML/ODF/XML/EPUB/DIF/XPS/iWork/HTML parsers use 'parseSAX(..., new OfflineContentHandler(...), context)'. The only other occurrence without an outermost OfflineContentHandler is NetworkParser (line 131), where the guard is nested under TeeContentHandler and the parsed data is a configured remote endpoint response, so the XLSX case is the stronger, client-reachable one.

records.claim_title: Unescaped archive file name interpolated into `bash -c` in FileUtil.unTar allows OS command execution during YARN resource localization
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: FileUtil.unTarUsingTar() builds a shell command string (` gzip -dc '<in>' | (cd '<dir>' ; tar -xf ... )`) and executes it via `{"bash","-c",...}` using makeShellPath(), which simply returns the file/directory name without shell escaping (FileUtil.java:514-516). Only single quotes are added around the names, so a `'` inside a name terminates the quoted string and the remainder is interpreted as shell syntax. The attacker-controlled component is the file name taken from a YARN LocalResource URL: FSDownload.call() derives both the final destination (`dst_work/<name>`) and the temp copy (`tmp_<name>`) from `resource.getResource().toPath().getName()`, and dispatches to FileUtil.unTar() when that name ends in .tar.gz/.tgz/.tar.

records.claim_title: Unsafe YAML deserialization in SnakeYamlEngine (request-body parsing with unrestricted SnakeYAML `new Yaml().load`)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SnakeYamlEngine.fromString parses attacker-supplied request-body text with SnakeYAML's default (non-restricted) API: `return (T) new Yaml().load(content);` (SnakeYamlEngine.java:46-49). The default `Yaml()`/`Constructor` path of the pinned SnakeYAML 1.17 (pippo-snakeyaml/pom.xml:17-33, `<snakeyaml.version>1.17</snakeyaml.version>`) resolves and instantiates arbitrary Java classes named by global YAML type tags instead of being limited to plain data types (no `SafeConstructor`, no `LoaderOptions`/type restrictions, and no result-type filter on `classOfT`). The engine is auto-registered for `application/x-yaml` (and suffix `yaml`) by SnakeYamlInitializer.init (SnakeYamlInitializer.java:28-31) through the `@MetaInfServices`/ServiceLoader mechanism consumed in Application.init (Application.java:99-109), so any application that has this optional module on the classpath exposes an unsafe deserializer through the framework's normal body-parsing API.

records.claim_title: Pre-auth AMQP 0-8/0-9/0-9-1 decoding allocates byte arrays from unvalidated 4-byte length fields (remote OOM / broker termination)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In broker-core EncodingUtils, length-prefixed values are decoded by reading a 4-byte unsigned length and immediately allocating `new byte[(int) length]` without verifying that the declared length is actually available in the remaining buffer: readLongString (lines 230-244), readLongstr (lines 256-270) and readBytes (lines 316-330). A declared length up to 0x7FFFFFFF therefore forces an allocation of up to ~2 GiB (or a NegativeArraySizeException for lengths > 2^31-1) from a tiny frame, and the missing check is asymmetric with the guarded short-string reader AMQShortString.readAMQShortStringAsBytes (lines 86-97), which does enforce `length > buffer.remaining()`; QpidByteBuffer.view (MultiQpidByteBuffer lines 953-957) likewise validates only the outer table length, not inner value lengths.

records.claim_title: Path traversal (Zip Slip) in obr:source JAR extraction allows arbitrary file write outside the chosen directory
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: FileUtil.unjar validates JAR entry names only against absolute paths (entry name startsWith "/") and never rejects relative ".." path segments. records.claim_title: HTTP/2 control-frame responses are unbounded: Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder is never installed in any pipeline
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: codec-http2 ships a defensive wrapper, `Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder`, that counts outstanding control frames it writes (PING ACK, SETTINGS ACK, RST_STREAM) and closes the connection with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM once a configured maximum is reached (file lines 25-113, especially `handleOutstandingControlFrames`, lines 88-112). However, the class is dead code: a repository-wide text search finds no `new Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder(...)` and no other reference to the type, so it is never wrapped around the connection encoder. All encoder construction paths install only `DefaultHttp2ConnectionEncoder` (optionally wrapped by `StreamBufferingEncoder`): `AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.buildFromConnection` lines 470-486, `Http2FrameCodecBuilder.build` lines 179-186, `Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder.build` lines 205-212. No `maxOutstandingControlFrames` option exists on any builder either. At the same time `DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder` unconditionally writes a reply for attacker-triggered control frames: `onSettingsRead` writes a SETTINGS ACK whenever `settingsReceivedConsumer == null` (the default, since `autoAckSettingsFrame = true`, `AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder` line 108), lines 466-480; `onPingRead` writes a PING ACK whenever `autoAckPing` is true (default `autoAckPingFrame = true`, line 109), lines 482-489; RST_STREAM replies are also emitted by lifecycle error handling. Because these writes are never bounded or short-circuited, a peer that never reads the socket causes the control-frame responses and their channel promises/listeners to accumulate in Netty's outbound buffer until memory is exhausted.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: WsFrameBase.processRemainingHeader() decodes the 8-byte extended payload length with byteArrayToLong() but never applies RFC 6455's rule that the most significant bit of a 64-bit length MUST be 0 (lines 261-265). byteArrayToLong() only rejects len > 8 (lines 667-678), so a length whose first byte is >= 0x80 yields a negative long. The subsequent control-frame guard is payloadLength > 125 (line 267), which is false for negative values, so the frame proceeds to State.DATA (line 281). On the server side the UnmaskTransformation.getMoreData() loop condition payloadWritten < payloadLength (line 985) is immediately false, and the method returns TransformationResult.OVERFLOW (lines 999-1002) without consuming input or advancing payloadWritten. processDataText() (lines 405-449) and processDataBinary() with a Partial handler (lines 504-530) then re-invoke getMoreData() in a while (!END_OF_FRAME) loop while inputBuffer.remaining() > 0, which never changes, producing an infinite CPU-bound loop. A correct implementation would throw a protocol-error WsIOException when payloadLength < 0 after line 264.

records.claim_title: Unbounded/negative array allocation from unvalidated CiphertextHeader length fields (decryption DoS)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: CiphertextHeader.decode() parses the cleartext header with only one validation: the total header length must be non-negative. records.claim_title: Infinite Loop Denial of Service in NioZipEncoding#encode on Incomplete Surrogate Input
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In NioZipEncoding#encode(String), the while loop checks 'cb.remaining() > 0' and calls 'enc.encode(cb, out, false)'. Passing 'false' for endOfInput causes Java's CharsetEncoder to return CoderResult.UNDERFLOW when an incomplete surrogate sequence (e.g. an isolated high surrogate at the end of the input CharBuffer) is encountered, without advancing cb's position. The loop body only handles 'isUnmappable()', 'isMalformed()', and 'isOverflow()', leaving CoderResult.UNDERFLOW unhandled. Because cb.remaining() remains greater than 0 and the encoder state is unchanged, the loop iterates indefinitely, consuming 100% CPU. Similarly, encodeFully only handles isOverflow and spins infinitely if any other non-advancing result is returned.

records.claim_title: Infinite loop in NioZipEncoding.encode() caused by unhandled CharsetEncoder UNDERFLOW on incomplete surrogate sequences
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In NioZipEncoding.encode(final String name), the method invokes enc.encode(cb, out, false) inside a 'while (cb.remaining() > 0)' loop with endOfInput explicitly set to false, even though the full input string is already wrapped in CharBuffer cb. When the input ends with an incomplete sequence (such as an unpaired high surrogate), Java NIO's CharsetEncoder returns CoderResult.UNDERFLOW without consuming the high surrogate, expecting additional input in a subsequent buffer. The loop handles unmappable/malformed (by surrogate encoding) and overflow (by buffer expansion), but provides no branch or handling for underflow while cb.remaining() > 0. Consequently, cb.remaining() remains positive, the loop repeats indefinitely, and the encoder repeatedly returns UNDERFLOW. Additionally, TarUtils.formatNameBytes truncates long file names with name.substring(0, --len) in a loop, which can split a surrogate pair and generate an unpaired high surrogate at the end of the string.

records.claim_title: Denial of Service (infinite loop and CPU exhaustion) via crafted multipart boundary in MultipartStream (CVE-2014-0050)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In MultipartStream, the constructor initializes internal buffer structures based on a fixed or caller-supplied buffer size (default DEFAULT_BUFSIZE = 4096 bytes) but never validates that bufSize is larger than boundaryLength (boundary.length + BOUNDARY_PREFIX.length). In FileUploadBase.getBoundary, the boundary string is extracted from the Content-Type header without length restrictions. When a boundary parameter of length >= 4092 bytes is provided, boundaryLength and keepRegion meet or exceed bufSize. In ItemInputStream.makeAvailable(), once the buffer fills to capacity (tail == bufSize), findSeparator() cannot find the delimiter and returns -1, pad is assigned tail - head (bufSize), and available() returns 0. The method then enters an infinite loop repeatedly calling input.read(buffer, tail, bufSize - tail) with len == 0, which per Java InputStream contract returns 0 bytes endlessly without blocking or throwing an exception.

records.claim_title: Infinite Loop and CPU Exhaustion via Long Boundary in MultipartStream (CVE-2014-0050)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `MultipartStream.java`, `MultipartStream(InputStream, byte[], int, ProgressNotifier)` initializes the internal buffer with `bufSize` (defaulting to 4096 bytes via `DEFAULT_BUFSIZE`) and computes `boundaryLength = boundary.length + BOUNDARY_PREFIX.length` without checking that `bufSize` is large enough to contain the boundary plus required delimiters and data. When `keepRegion` (`boundary.length + 4`) is greater than or equal to `bufSize` (e.g. boundary length >= 4092 bytes under default buffer size), `ItemInputStream.findSeparator()` sets `pad = tail - head = bufSize` when the boundary is not found. Consequently, in `ItemInputStream.makeAvailable()`, `tail` equals `bufSize`, making `bufSize - tail == 0`. The method then enters an infinite `for (;;)` loop calling `input.read(buffer, tail, 0)`. In Java, reading 0 bytes returns 0 immediately without reading from the stream or blocking, leaving `tail` unchanged, `available()` returning 0, and the loop spinning indefinitely at 100% CPU.

records.claim_title: Infinite Loop in PixelParserBitFields leading to Denial of Service via Zero Bitmask
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In PixelParserBitFields.java, the getMaskShift(int mask) method uses a while loop `while ((0x1 & mask) == 0)` to count trailing zeroes by repeatedly shifting mask right (`mask = 0x7fffffff & (mask >> 1)`). Consequently, when redMask, greenMask, or blueMask is 0 (as supplied by an untrusted BMP file with BI_BITFIELDS compression), getMaskShift enters an infinite loop.

records.claim_title: Improper Path Traversal Validation in FilenameUtils.normalize and FilenameUtils.concat via UNC Prefix Parsing

records.claim_title: Authentication and Authorization Bypass via Context Path Semicolon Truncation in WebUtils (CVE-2016-6802)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `WebUtils.decodeAndCleanUriString`, Shiro removes extraneous path parameters by locating the first semicolon (`int semicolonIndex = uri.indexOf(';')`) and truncating the entire remainder of the URI string (`uri.substring(0, semicolonIndex)`). This assumes semicolons appear only as trailing parameters on the final URI resource (such as `;jsessionid`). However, RFC 3986 and Servlet specifications allow matrix parameters on any path segment, including the context path segment. When an application is deployed under a non-root servlet context path (e.g., `/myapp`), a request such as `GET /myapp;foo/admin/users HTTP/1.1` causes `decodeAndCleanUriString` to truncate everything after `/myapp`. Subsequently, `WebUtils.getPathWithinApplication` computes `requestUri.substring(contextPath.length())`, which results in `""` and resolves to `"/"`. While Shiro evaluates the path within the application as `"/"`, the Servlet container parses matrix parameters on a per-segment basis, stripping `;foo` from the context path segment and dispatching the request to the `/admin/users` servlet. Because Shiro checks filter matching against `"/"` instead of `/admin/users`, the filter chain configured for `/admin/**` is bypassed.

records.claim_title: XSS Validation and Sanitization Bypass in getValidHref and isValidHref via HTML5 Entity Encoding
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In XSSFilterImpl.isValidHref and XSSAPIImpl.getValidHref, the methods attempt to decode URL and XML encodings prior to validation using StringEscapeUtils.unescapeXml(). Because unescapeXml only decodes basic XML 1.0 entities and numeric references, HTML5 named character references like ':' are not decoded. records.claim_title: CookieInterceptor ClassLoader Manipulation Bypass via Whitespace and Incomplete Exclude Patterns (CVE-2014-0116 / S2-023)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In Apache Struts 2.3.16.2, CookieInterceptor was updated to mitigate ClassLoader manipulation by validating cookie names and values against ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN. However, ACCEPTED_PATTERN in CookieInterceptor allows whitespace ('\\s'), while CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN ("(.*\\.|^|.*|\\[('|\"))class(\\.|('|\")]|\\[).*") expects 'class' to be immediately followed by a dot, bracket, or quote without whitespace. Because OGNL parses expressions ignoring whitespace, an attacker can supply a cookie name such as "class ['classLoader']..." or "class .classLoader..." which matches ACCEPTED_PATTERN but evades CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN. Furthermore, CookieInterceptor only checks CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN and fails to check the remaining patterns in ExcludedPatterns.EXCLUDED_PATTERNS (^session\\..*, ^request\\..*, ^application\\..*), and passes un-sandboxed expressions directly to ValueStack.setValue().

Rather than extracting the peer's X.509 certificate and verifying that the Common Name (CN) or Subject Alternative Name (SAN) matches the target hostname, they only check whether the target URL hostname (passed as the String hostname argument) matches the configured whitelist or regular expression. Because the client initiates the connection to its configured CAS server URL, that parameter always matches the configured whitelist or pattern, causing verify() to return true regardless of the certificate presented by the remote server.

records.claim_title: MFA Bypass via Spring MVC Mass Assignment in TotpMfaEndpoint
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Spring MVC mass assignment / parameter binding vulnerability on the MFA verification handler. In `TotpMfaEndpoint.validateCode`, the method parameter `credentials` is declared with `@ModelAttribute("uaaMfaCredentials") UserGoogleMfaCredentials credentials`. In Spring MVC, `@ModelAttribute` triggers automatic data binding from incoming HTTP request parameters to the target object. Because `UserGoogleMfaCredentials` provides a public `setSecretKey(String)` method and no field restrictions (`@InitBinder` / `setAllowedFields` / `setDisallowedFields`) are declared, an attacker can supply an arbitrary `secretKey` parameter in the `POST /login/mfa/verify.do` request. This overwrites the legitimate secret key in memory before `mfaCredentialsProvisioning.isValidCode(credentials, codeValue)` verifies the submitted TOTP code against `credentials.getSecretKey()`.

records.claim_title: OS Command Injection via Incomplete Shell Argument Quoting and Escaping in Commandline
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Commandline executes external commands by concatenating executable paths and arguments into a single shell command line passed to /bin/sh -c (BourneShell) or cmd.exe /X /C (CmdShell), rather than passing arguments directly as an array to Runtime.getRuntime().exec() without a shell. The argument quoting and escaping implementation in Shell and StringUtils.quoteAndEscape is flawed: (1) In StringUtils.quoteAndEscape (lines 2314-2318), any argument that begins and ends with the quote character (e.g. single quotes in BourneShell) is treated as already quoted and returned without any escaping, allowing attackers to inject closing quotes and arbitrary shell commands; (2) BourneShell.BASH_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS omits newline (\n), allowing unquoted arguments containing newlines to execute subsequent lines as commands; (3) CmdShell does not define custom escape characters or trigger characters, leaving cmd metacharacters (&, |, <, >, ^) unquoted and unescaped.

records.claim_title: Partial Path Traversal Boundary Bypass in DefaultValidator Directory Path Validation
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `DefaultValidator.java` (line 460), the method `getValidDirectoryPath` verifies whether the directory is inside the parent directory using `dir.getCanonicalPath().startsWith(parent.getCanonicalPath())`. Because `File.getCanonicalPath()` returns a string without a trailing file separator (e.g., `/var/app/uploads`), calling `startsWith` performs string prefix matching rather than directory hierarchy validation. As a result, any existing sibling directory whose name starts with the parent directory name (such as `/var/app/uploads_admin` or `/var/app/uploads-backup`) evaluates to true and bypasses validation.

records.claim_title: Incomplete DTD and Entity Expansion Restriction in XmlFactory (XXE / Denial of Service)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In XmlFactory.java, the default XMLInputFactory initialization only sets XMLInputFactory.IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES to Boolean.FALSE (as an incomplete mitigation for dataformat-xml#190 / CVE-2016-3720). Because DTD processing remains enabled by default in StAX parsers, internal recursive entity declarations (Billion Laughs) and external DTD declarations/parameter entities are still processed. records.claim_title: Cryptographic Signature Verification Bypass via Two-Part Unsecured JWT in JWTDecoder
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In JWTDecoder.java, when verifier(s) are supplied to decode(), the method searches for a verifier matching header.algorithm. If the attacker provides an unsecured token (alg: 'none') or an algorithm not supported by any configured verifier, verifier resolves to null. In private decode(encodedJWT, header, parts, verifier), line 159 only enforces verifier presence if parts.length == 3, and line 164 only enforces signature presence if parts.length == 2 && verifier != null. Because parts.length == 2 and verifier == null, neither condition is met, no signature check is executed, and the forged token payload is deserialized and returned as valid.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `JWTDecoder.java`, two-part JWT strings formatted with a trailing dot (`header.payload.`) are accepted by `getParts` as valid tokens (`parts.length == 2`). records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In XStream.java, the field insecureWarning was overloaded to serve two incompatible functions: (1) indicating whether the security framework remains in its uninitialized/default state where InternalBlackList should block known dangerous types (EventHandler, LazyIterator, javax.crypto.*), and (2) gating the one-time console warning 'Security framework of XStream not initialized, XStream is probably vulnerable.' records.claim_title: HTTP/2 Header Value CRLF Injection Leading to HTTP Request Smuggling in ProxyHandler
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Undertow's HTTP/2 protocol implementation fails to validate header values against CR (0x0D) and LF (0x0A) characters as mandated by RFC 7540 Sections 8.1.2.6 ('Characters in field values MUST NOT contain CR or LF') and 10.3 ('Intermediaries that forward HTTP/2 requests to HTTP/1.1 MUST NOT permit CRLF sequences in header field values'). In Http2HeaderBlockParser.emitHeader, extensive validation is performed on header names, but header values are appended to the HeaderMap without character verification. Http2ReceiveListener.checkRequestHeaders only validates pseudo-headers and the TE header. records.claim_title: Argument and Environment Variable Injection via Embedded Null Characters in LinuxProcess
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `LinuxProcess.prepareProcess()`, command arguments are serialized into a single contiguous byte array (`argBlock`) where entries are separated by null bytes (`\0`), and passed alongside argument count `argc` (`args.length`) directly to JVM internal native methods (`Java_java_lang_ProcessImpl_forkAndExec` or `Java_java_lang_UNIXProcess_forkAndExec`) via JNA. The code explicitly references OpenJDK's `ProcessImpl.java#L71-L83`, but omits the security check present in OpenJDK (`if (cmdarray[i].indexOf('\u0000') >= 0) throw new IOException("embedded null character")`). Because OpenJDK's native `forkAndExec` reconstructs the argument vector `argv` by traversing `argBlock` with `p += strlen(p) + 1;` for `argc` iterations, any embedded null byte within an argument terminates `strlen(p)` prematurely. This promotes the remainder of the argument into an independent, injected command-line argument and shifts subsequent arguments, causing argument injection and parameter tampering.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: `RejectASTTransformsCustomizer` uses `RejectASTTransformsVisitor` (subclassing `ClassCodeVisitorSupport`) at `CompilePhase.CONVERSION` to detect and reject dangerous AST transform annotations like `@ASTTest`. records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: When DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled, primitive deserializers in StdDeserializer (_parseIntPrimitive, _parseBooleanPrimitive, etc.), BuilderBasedDeserializer, and StackTraceElementDeserializer do not verify whether the unwrapped token is another START_ARRAY before recursively calling parsing methods. Unlike StdDeserializer._deserializeWrappedValue (which guards against recursive array wrapping), these paths make unbounded recursive calls on nested arrays, exhausting stack frames and triggering java.lang.StackOverflowError. Furthermore, an attempted fix in BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray improperly invokes p.nextToken() a second time, leaving a 2-level array bypass.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: BeanDeserializer._deserializeFromArray and BuilderBasedDeserializer._deserializeFromArray override array unwrapping logic but fail to guard against nested JSON arrays when DeserializationFeature.UNWRAP_SINGLE_VALUE_ARRAYS is enabled. records.claim_title: X.509 Issuer vs Subject Principal Confusion Causing Certificate Validation Bypass and Caller Identity Spoofing
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert:
Confusion between X509Certificate.getIssuerX500Principal() and X509Certificate.getSubjectX500Principal() in Payara's certificate authentication logic:
1. In CertificateRealm.java (lines 245), getCertificateFromSubject compares the caller's principal (the certificate subject) against certificate.getIssuerX500Principal(). For CA-issued certificates, subject does not equal issuer, so lookup fails and validateSubjectViaAPI aborts without performing validation.
2. In CertificateCredentialImpl.java (line 71), getPrincipal() extracts the issuer principal instead of the subject principal, returning the CA's identity as the CallerPrincipal.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DBCPConnectionPool (and related controller services) defines the 'database-driver-locations' property with 'identifiesExternalResource(..., ResourceType.URL)' and 'dynamicallyModifiesClasspath(true)', allowing arbitrary remote HTTP/HTTPS URLs to be added to the component's InstanceClassLoader (URLClassLoader). records.claim_title: Insecure Symbolic Link Extraction and Arbitrary File Write / Permission Modification in AbstractUnArchiver
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile(), the path traversal (Zip Slip) validation only checks that targetFileName.getCanonicalFile().toPath().startsWith(canonicalDirPath). It completely omits validation for symlinkDestination, allowing symbolic links pointing outside the extraction directory to be created via SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(). Furthermore, extractFile() subsequent operations follow symbolic links: ArchiveEntryUtils.chmod(targetFileName, mode) modifies permissions on the symlink target, and if a dangling symlink entry is followed by a regular file entry of the same name, the canonical path check passes (because JDK canonicalization falls back to the parent directory inside the target when realpath fails on non-existent targets), causing Files.newOutputStream() to follow the symlink and write arbitrary content outside the destination directory.

records.claim_title: Insecure Deserialization of Untrusted XML in Filter Stream Parameter Parsing Leading to Remote Code Execution
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: DefaultXMLParser dynamically loads and initializes arbitrary classes specified in the 't' XML attribute via Class.forName(typeString, true, ...). records.claim_title: XSS Sanitization Bypass in SafeHtmlValidator via Parser Differential and Dropped Non-Element Nodes
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: SafeHtmlValidator parses the input fragment using Jsoup's XML parser (Parser.xmlParser()) instead of an HTML parser, and only extracts Element nodes via fragment.children() to append into document.body(). Due to parser differentials between XML and HTML5 specifications (particularly regarding processing instructions '<?...?>', comments '<!--...-->', and CDATA sections '<![CDATA[...]]>'), malicious script tags enclosed after intermediate '>' delimiters are parsed as non-Element XML nodes by Jsoup (such as XmlDeclaration or CDataNode). These non-Element nodes are omitted from fragment.children() and never appended to document.body(), leaving the document empty and causing Cleaner.isValid() to return true. In contrast, modern web browsers parse the content as HTML5, terminating the bogus comment on the first '>' delimiter and executing the subsequent script tag.

records.claim_title: Missing TLS Hostname Verification in Netty Client HTTP Transport (NettyHttpConduit)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: NettyHttpConduit relies on SslHandler initialized with an SSLEngine that lacks HTTPS endpoint identification algorithm configuration. Hostname verification logic (verifier.verify(url.getHost(), session)) is implemented exclusively inside getHttpsURLConnectionInfo(). However, HTTPConduit only calls getHttpsURLConnectionInfo() inside makeTrustDecision() if a MessageTrustDecider is explicitly set on the conduit or message. Under standard configurations, makeTrustDecision() bypasses this call, meaning the hostname is never verified during the TLS handshake or connection setup.

records.claim_title: SAML Identity Provider Signature Verification Bypass for Unsigned Responses in SAMLEndpoint
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In SAMLEndpoint.PostBinding.verifySignature, signature verification is bypassed if no <Signature> elements exist in the document (anyElementSigned == false) under the assumption that signature verification will be enforced on the assertion element later. However, in SAMLEndpoint.Binding.handleLoginResponse, the assertion signature is only verified if the assertion element explicitly contains a signature (signed == true) or if wantAssertionsSigned is enabled. Consequently, when an attacker submits an entirely unsigned SAML Response and Assertion to an Identity Provider with validateSignature enabled and wantAssertionsSigned disabled (default), neither the response-level nor assertion-level signature check is ever executed.

records.claim_title: Incomplete HTTP/2 Overhead Limiting Leading to Denial of Service (CVE-2019-10072)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: The HTTP/2 frame overhead tracking mechanism (overheadCount / overheadCountFactor introduced in CVE-2019-0199) is incomplete. First, in Http2UpgradeHandler.upgradeDispatch(), frames are continuously read in a while (true) loop and the overheadCount limit check (overheadCount.get() > 0) is only evaluated after the read loop terminates, allowing an uninterrupted stream of frames to monopolize the processing thread. Second, overheadCount only tracks PRIORITY, SETTINGS, and PING frames, while RST_STREAM (reset()) and WINDOW_UPDATE (incrementWindowSize()) frames do not increment overheadCount. Third, headersStart() and startRequestBodyFrame() call reduceOverheadCount(), allowing an attacker to open streams (reducing the counter) and immediately reset them (without increasing the counter), driving overheadCount further negative and bypassing overhead protection entirely.

records.ground_truth_vulnerability: Netty HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader accepts whitespace between request header name and colon
records.ground_truth: Netty HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader accepts whitespace between request header name and colon
records.claim_title: HTTP Request Smuggling via whitespace tolerance before header colon in HttpObjectDecoder
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader, the parser breaks the header name scan upon encountering any whitespace character (if (ch == ':' || Character.isWhitespace(ch))) and then scans forward in a secondary loop to locate a subsequent colon. This causes trailing whitespace between the header name and the colon (e.g., 'Transfer-Encoding : chunked') to be stripped and discarded rather than rejected. According to RFC 7230 §3.2.4, no whitespace is allowed between the header field-name and colon, and servers must reject such messages with a 400 Bad Request. Netty instead treats the header as valid 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked', creating an interpretation discrepancy with RFC-compliant frontend proxies.

records.claim_title: Apache CXF OAuth2 / OpenID Connect Token Service Fails to Validate Client ID on Token Refresh (CVE-2019-12419)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RFC 6749 Section 6 mandates that when refreshing an access token, the authorization server must authenticate the client and ensure that the refresh token was issued to the authenticated client. In Apache CXF's OAuth2 and OpenID Connect implementation, RefreshTokenGrantHandler.createAccessToken delegates directly to OAuthDataProvider.refreshAccessToken(client, refreshToken, requestedScopes). In AbstractOAuthDataProvider.refreshAccessToken, the ServerAccessToken / RefreshToken is retrieved using the refresh token key, but the data provider never validates whether currentRefreshToken.getClient() matches the requesting client. Instead, doRefreshAccessToken calls createNewAccessToken(client, oldRefreshToken.getSubject()), issuing new tokens bound to the attacker's client with the victim user's subject. In OpenID Connect environments, IdTokenResponseFilter then signs a new ID token for the attacker's client asserting identity of the victim subject.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: HttpObjectDecoder and HttpUtil fail to enforce RFC 7230 §3.3.2 and §3.3.3 framing constraints. records.claim_title: Denial of Service via Uncaught JVM Crash when Deserializing 'void' Type (CVE-2017-7957)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `Primitives.java`, `Void.TYPE` (`void.class`) is registered in `NAMED_PRIMITIVE` as `'void'`. When an XML document contains `<void/>`, `DefaultMapper.realClass('void')` resolves it to `void.class`. `PrimitiveTypePermission.PRIMITIVES` permits `void.class` because `void.class.isPrimitive()` returns true, and `setupSecurity()` in `XStream.java` enables this permission by default without denying `void`. `ReflectionConverter` then handles `void.class` and delegates instantiation to `SunLimitedUnsafeReflectionProvider.newInstance(void.class)`, which directly calls `unsafe.allocateInstance(void.class)`. In HotSpot JVMs, passing the pseudo-primitive `void` type to `Unsafe.allocateInstance` results in an illegal memory dereference in native code, causing a fatal segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) and crashing the JVM process.

records.claim_title: NULL Pointer Dereference and Missing Validation in XMSS/XMSS^MT Key Retrieval via BDS Deserialization
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In BCXMSSPrivateKey and BCXMSSMTPrivateKey, deserialization of the BDS state from PrivateKeyInfo using XMSSUtil.deserialize() passes the reconstructed BDS/BDSStateMap object directly to keyBuilder.withBDSState(...) without calling setXMSS(...) or validate(). Because the 'wotsPlus' field in BDS is declared transient and BDS does not define readObject(), 'wotsPlus' remains null after deserialization. When the key is later used to sign (via XMSSSigner or XMSSMTSigner), bdsState.getNextState() dereferences wotsPlus, triggering a NullPointerException. Additionally, BDS integrity validation (validate()) is completely omitted during JCA key retrieval, allowing corrupted or tampered BDS trees to be loaded without early detection.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In org.postgresql.util.ObjectFactory.instantiate, the driver dynamically resolves Class.forName(classname) and invokes ctor.newInstance(args) without checking whether the class implements or extends the expected interface or class (such as javax.net.SocketFactory, javax.net.ssl.SSLSocketFactory, javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier, or javax.security.auth.callback.CallbackHandler) beforehand. records.claim_title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator Worksheet Parsing
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet(), sheetInputStream is parsed using XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX(sheetInputStream, handler, parseContext) where handler is an instance of XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer (which extends DefaultHandler). In Apache Tika's architecture, SAXParserFactory does not disable external entity features by itself and instead relies on wrapping handlers in OfflineContentHandler to neutralize external entity resolution via resolveEntity(). Unlike all other SAX parse invocations across the repository (and even workbook parsing in line 200 of the same class), the worksheet handler at line 342 is not wrapped in OfflineContentHandler, nor does XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer override resolveEntity(). As a result, DefaultHandler.resolveEntity() returns null, causing the underlying XML parser to resolve external DTDs and external entities, leading to XML External Entity (XXE) injection.

records.claim_title: OS Command Injection in FileUtil.unTarUsingTar during Archive Extraction
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In FileUtil.unTarUsingTar, command strings for bash are constructed using direct string concatenation of file paths (inFile and untarDir) returned by FileUtil.makeShellPath. For uncompressed tar archives (and .tgz archives), inFile is not enclosed in quotes, allowing immediate shell metacharacter injection. For gzipped archives, single quotes are appended around paths but without escaping existing single quotes, allowing command injection via '$(...)' or command separators. The constructed command string is then passed to 'bash -c' via ShellCommandExecutor.

records.claim_title: Overall/Read Authorization Bypass via SecurityRealm and User DescriptorByNameOwner Dynamic Routing (CVE-2018-1000861)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Jenkins exempts the '/securityRealm' prefix from Overall/Read authorization checks in ALWAYS_READABLE_PATHS (Jenkins.java). HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm defines a public method 'getUser(String id)' that retrieves or creates a User object for any requested identifier without authentication or permission checks. User implements DescriptorByNameOwner and exposes 'getDescriptorByName(String className)', which delegates directly to Jenkins.getDescriptorByName without access control. records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Overall/Read Permission Bypass and Arbitrary Descriptor Access via /securityRealm/ Whitelist and DescriptorByNameOwner
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Jenkins defines ALWAYS_READABLE_PATHS to exempt authentication-related URLs from mandatory Overall/Read permission checks (isSubjectToMandatoryReadPermissionCheck), whitelisting the prefix '/securityRealm'. Under this exempt prefix, HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm.getUser(String id) unconditionally invokes User.getById(id, true) with create=true and without permission checks, creating user records on disk for arbitrary usernames. Furthermore, User implements DescriptorByNameOwner, which exposes getDescriptorByName(String className) without access control. Through Stapler URL dynamic dispatch, unauthenticated requests to /securityRealm/user/<username>/descriptorByName/<DescriptorId>/ can reach and invoke methods on any registered Descriptor in Jenkins, bypassing authentication and overall read restrictions (SECURITY-595 / SECURITY-1072, CVE-2018-1000861 / CVE-2018-1000862).

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Denial of Service via Malformed AMQP 0-10 Frames Causing Uncaught NullPointerException and Resource Leak
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In ServerAssembler.frame(), when receiving a frame where isFirstFrame() is false without a prior first frame for the segment, getSegment(frame) returns null, and ServerAssembler directly invokes frames.add(frame) without a null check, throwing a NullPointerException. Similarly, in assemble(), receiving HEADER or BODY frames without a preceding incomplete COMMAND results in getIncompleteCommand(channel) returning null and subsequent dereference throwing a NullPointerException. Because AMQPConnection_0_10Impl.onReceive() only catches IllegalArgumentException and IllegalStateException, and NonBlockingConnection.doWork() only catches IOException and ConnectionScopedRuntimeException, the NullPointerException propagates uncaught, terminating the scheduler thread execution abruptly. Crucially, this bypasses connection cleanup, clearScheduled(), and selector deregistration, permanently leaking the socket channel and file descriptor.

records.claim_title: Bypass of User Authorization and Impersonation Checks in HBase REST Server due to Unused RESTServletContainer
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `RESTServer.java`, `loginServerPrincipal(userProvider, conf)` returns `Pair<FilterHolder, Class<? extends ServletContainer>>`, where the second element is `RESTServletContainer.class` when client authentication is configured. However, in `RESTServer.main()`, only `pair.getFirst()` (`authFilter`) is retrieved. `pair.getSecond()` is completely ignored, and `RESTServer` hardcodes `ServletHolder sh = new ServletHolder(new ServletContainer(application));`. Because `RESTServletContainer` is never instantiated or registered with Jetty, its overridden `service()` method is never executed, and `servlet.setEffectiveUser(...)` is never called. Consequently, `ConnectionCache.getCurrentConnection()` defaults to `ConnectionCache.realUserName` (the HBase service superuser) for all requests, causing all operations across all authenticated users to execute with full superuser privileges.

records.claim_title: Incomplete Path Traversal (Zip Slip) Protection in KAR Archive Extraction (CVE-2019-0226)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In Kar.java, the extract() method unpacks entries from a KAR (Zip/Jar) archive using a naive blacklist filter: `entry.getName().contains("..") || entry.getName().contains("%2e%2e")`. When constructing destination files using `new File(repoDir, path)` or `new File(resourceDir, path)`, it fails to verify that the canonical path of the destination file actually starts with the canonical path of the intended target directory. On platforms such as Windows, paths specifying a drive letter (e.g. 'C:/...') or root-relative slashes resolve to absolute filesystem locations outside the target folder, bypassing the blacklist and writing files to arbitrary filesystem locations.

records.claim_title: Insecure Shared Temporary Directory Creation Allowing Local Code Execution and Information Disclosure in WebInfConfiguration and MultiPartInputStreamParser (CVE-2020-27216)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In WebInfConfiguration.java, when no specific temporary directory or work directory is configured, Jetty defaults to creating its temporary workspace directly inside the system shared temporary directory (java.io.tmpdir, typically /tmp). When creating the temporary directory (makeTempDirectory), Jetty either computes a completely predictable directory name based on static webapp metadata (host, port, war name, context path) when persisted, or calls File.createTempFile(temp, '.dir', parent), immediately deletes the created file with tmpDir.delete(), and then creates a directory with tmpDir.mkdirs(). This introduces a Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use (TOCTOU) race condition and relies on the default process umask without setting POSIX owner-only (0700) permissions. In configureTempDirectory, if the directory already exists and persistence is enabled, Jetty blindly reuses it if dir.canWrite() is true. During deployment (unpack), the entire WAR file—including executable bytecode in WEB-INF/classes and JSP files—is extracted into extractedWebAppDir = new File(context.getTempDirectory(), 'webapp'). A collocated user can pre-create or tamper with this directory, leading to arbitrary code execution as the Jetty user (CVE-2020-27216). MultiPartInputStreamParser exhibits an identical flaw by falling back to java.io.tmpdir with world-readable permissions for multipart file uploads.

During deployment (unpack), the entire WAR file—including executable bytecode in WEB-INF/classes and JSP files—is extracted into extractedWebAppDir = new File(context.getTempDirectory(), 'webapp'). A collocated user can pre-create or tamper with this directory, leading to arbitrary code execution as the Jetty user (CVE-2020-27216). records.claim_title: WebSocket Frame Payload Length Validation Failure Leads to Infinite Loop Denial of Service (CVE-2020-13935)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In WsFrameBase.java, when reading an 8-byte WebSocket frame payload length (header payload length indicator 127), Tomcat does not validate that the most significant bit is zero as required by RFC 6455 Section 5.2. Furthermore, in byteArrayToLong(), shifts are executed on 32-bit integers without widening (b[i] & 0xFF) to a 64-bit long prior to shifting (e.g. ((b[i] & 0xFF) << shift) where shift >= 32 wraps modulo 32 and shift=56 shifts 24 bits), causing the resulting payloadLength to become negative. When payloadLength is negative, UnmaskTransformation.getMoreData() skips the extraction loop (payloadWritten < payloadLength is false), does not consume any bytes, and returns TransformationResult.OVERFLOW. In processDataText(), OVERFLOW causes an inner decode loop to underflow and break, repeatedly re-invoking getMoreData() in an infinite outer loop that never advances inputBuffer or terminates.

records.claim_title: Infinite Loop and CPU Exhaustion via Crafted Multipart Boundary in MultipartStream (CVE-2014-0050)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: MultipartStream does not validate that the configured buffer size (bufSize, defaulting to 4096 bytes) is larger than the boundary length (boundary.length + BOUNDARY_PREFIX.length + 1). When an incoming request specifies a boundary parameter whose length meets or exceeds the buffer capacity (e.g., >= 4092 bytes with DEFAULT_BUFSIZE = 4096), keepRegion equals or exceeds bufSize. During stream parsing in ItemInputStream.findSeparator(), pad is set to the full buffer length, causing available() to evaluate to 0. Consequently, in ItemInputStream.makeAvailable(), input.read(buffer, tail, bufSize - tail) is invoked with len = 0 (since tail == bufSize), which returns 0 according to InputStream specification without reading data or signaling EOF. The enclosing for(;;) loop never terminates and available() remains 0, resulting in an unescapable infinite loop.

records.claim_title: Infinite Loop and Denial of Service in PixelParserBitFields via Zero Bitfield Mask
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In PixelParserBitFields.java, the helper method getMaskShift(int mask) contains a loop `while ((0x1 & mask) == 0)` that shifts mask to the right to find trailing zeroes. records.claim_title: Path Traversal via Improper UNC Prefix Handling in FilenameUtils.normalize and concat
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength(String), any path starting with two separator characters followed by a non-empty string and a third separator is parsed as a Windows UNC path (e.g. `//server/`). When the server segment is `..` (such as `//../foo`), getPrefixLength incorrectly returns 5 (`//../`). Because doNormalize only checks for `..` tokens starting after the prefix (`prefix + 2`), the traversal sequence is retained. Furthermore, FilenameUtils.concat treats any positive prefix length as an absolute path and discards the basePath entirely, returning the un-sanitized traversal path.

records.claim_title: Target Host Misinterpretation in URIUtils.extractHost via Malformed Authority Component (CVE-2020-13956)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In URIUtils.extractHost(final URI uri), when standard URI parsing fails to produce a host (uri.getHost() == null), HttpClient implements fallback parsing on uri.getAuthority(). The fallback logic locates user credentials using host.indexOf('@') (the first '@') rather than the last '@'. Furthermore, when extracting the port suffix, it finds the first colon (host.indexOf(':')), parses digits following it, and truncates the host with host.substring(0, colon). When presented with a malformed authority containing multiple '@' characters and an embedded port (such as 'user@attacker.com:80@victim.com' or 'foo@internal.corp:80@attacker.com'), everything after the port number is silently discarded, causing HttpClient to select an unintended target host.

records.claim_title: Uncontrolled Recursion / Denial of Service via KeyInfoReference and RetrievalMethod Reference Cycles in Key Resolvers
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Incomplete cycle detection and validation between KeyInfoReferenceResolver and RetrievalMethodResolver. KeyInfoReferenceResolver.validateReference() only checks whether the referent KeyInfo contains another KeyInfoReference, but does not check whether it contains a RetrievalMethod. RetrievalMethodResolver only checks whether the target element is a RetrievalMethod (and only detects direct 2-element cycles when secureValidation is disabled), failing to recognize KeyInfoReference elements. Furthermore, KeyInfoReferenceResolver fails to propagate the secureValidation flag to newly constructed referent KeyInfo instances. As a result, cross-referencing between RetrievalMethod and KeyInfoReference creates an infinite resolution loop.

records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: XSSFilterImpl.isValidHref() and XSSAPIImpl.getValidHref() rely on StringEscapeUtils.unescapeXml() to canonicalize URLs prior to regex validation against onsiteURL/offsiteURL. Because StringEscapeUtils.unescapeXml() only decodes XML 1.0 entities and does not resolve HTML5 named character references such as :, protocols like javascript: or data: retain : instead of the forbidden literal colon (:). records.claim_title: ClassLoader Manipulation via Incomplete Cookie Name Validation in CookieInterceptor (CVE-2014-0116)
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: CookieInterceptor uses ACCEPTED_PATTERN = '[a-zA-Z0-9\\.\\]\\[_\'\\s]+' to validate cookie names, which allows whitespace characters. It attempts to block ClassLoader access using ExcludedPatterns.CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN ('(.*\\.|^|.*|\\[(\'|\"))class(\\.|(\'|\")]|\\[).*'). Because CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN requires 'class' to be immediately followed by a dot, bracket, or quote token, inserting whitespace after 'class' (such as 'class .classLoader' or 'class [\'classLoader\']') bypasses CLASS_ACCESS_PATTERN while matching ACCEPTED_PATTERN. The cookie name is then passed directly to ValueStack.setValue(), where OGNL parses expressions ignoring whitespace around property access tokens and navigates to the ClassLoader without denyMethodExecution or property exclusion protections.

records.claim_title: Unauthenticated Remote Application Deployment and Code Execution via ServerServlet in tomee-webapp
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: In `tomee/tomee-webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml`, a `<security-constraint>` is declared for `ServerServlet` covering `<url-pattern>/ejb/*</url-pattern>` without an `<auth-constraint>`. Under Java Servlet specification semantics, an explicit `<security-constraint>` lacking an `<auth-constraint>` makes the matched URL pattern publicly accessible, overriding the `<auth-constraint>` defined on `/*`. Consequently, unauthenticated HTTP requests reach `ServerServlet`, which delegates directly to `EjbDaemon`. Because built-in system beans such as `DeployerEjb` (`openejb/Deployer`) lack method authorization constraints (defaulting to unchecked/permit-all permissions in JACC), unauthenticated callers can invoke `DeployerEjb.deploy(...)` to write and deploy arbitrary WAR archives.

records.claim_title: Broken SSL/TLS Hostname Verification in RegexHostnameVerifier and WhitelistHostnameVerifier Allows MitM Spoofing
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: RegexHostnameVerifier and WhitelistHostnameVerifier implement javax.net.ssl.HostnameVerifier, but their verify(String hostname, SSLSession session) methods ignore the SSLSession argument and fail to verify that the server's X.509 certificate (CN or subjectAltName) matches the requested hostname. Instead, both implementations only verify that the destination hostname matches a preconfigured regular expression or whitelist string. Consequently, any valid SSL/TLS certificate from any trusted CA is accepted, disabling certificate-to-host identity binding.

records.claim_title: OS Command Injection via Flawed Shell Argument Quoting and Escaping in Commandline
records.claim_root_cause_or_alert: Commandline.execute() executes external commands by invoking the host operating system's shell (/bin/sh -c on POSIX systems via BourneShell; cmd.exe /X /C on Windows via CmdShell) and assembling executable and arguments into a single shell command string, rather than passing arguments directly as individual process arguments. Argument quoting and escaping relies on StringUtils.quoteAndEscape(...), which suffers from critical flaws: (1) Lines 2314-2318 of StringUtils.java check if source starts and ends with quoteChar without 'force' enabled; if so, it assumes the argument is already safely quoted and returns it unmodified without escaping internal quotes or verifying quote balancing. An attacker supplying an argument such as '''; id; echo ''' (on POSIX) or '\"&calc.exe&\"' (on Windows) completely bypasses quote escaping, allowing command separators (; or &) to execute injected shell commands. (2) In BourneShell.java (lines 32-48), BASH_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS omits newline (\n), tab (\t), and carriage return (\r). An argument containing a newline without single quotes is returned completely unquoted, allowing newline-separated shell commands to be executed by /bin/sh. (3) In CmdShell.java, DEFAULT_QUOTING_TRIGGER_CHARS is only {' '}, and double quotes are not escaped (isDoubleQuotedArgumentEscaped() is false), permitting metacharacter injection via & or | when spaces are absent.
